units.title: Start Here — What is React and Why Does it Exist?

lessons.name: What is React and why does it exist?
lessons.desc: Without React: updating the DOM manually is slow, tedious, and error-prone at scale. React solves this with a component model where you describe what the UI should look like, and React figures out how to update the DOM efficiently. Built by Facebook in 2013.
lessons.q: What problem does React solve? What was wrong with updating the DOM manually?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between React the library and React DOM? Why are they separate packages?
terms: tum batate ho "screen aisi dikhni chahiye" — kaise karna hai wo React sochta hai
tum step-by-step batate ho — ye element pakdo, ye text badlo, ye class hatao
UI ek function ka result hai jiska input state hai
lessons.what:
Definition: React ek JavaScript library hai jo UI banane ke liye hai. Iska core idea ek line mein — UI = f(state). Tum state badalte ho, React screen ko us state se match kar deta hai.

Vanilla JS mein tum DOM ko haath se update karte ho. React mein tum sirf data badalte ho.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant mein order dena. Imperative = kitchen mein ghus ke bolna "gas on karo, tel daalo, pyaaz kaato". Declarative = waiter se bolna "ek paneer tikka". Kaise banega ye chef ka kaam.
lessons.why: Jaise app bada hota hai, manual DOM updates exponentially mushkil ho jaate hain. Ek data 5 jagah dikhta hai — badla to 5 jagah update karo, ek bhool gaye to UI aur data alag ho gaye (ye "state desync" bug sabse aam hai). React mein ye impossible hai kyunki UI hamesha state se derive hoti hai.

har keystroke pe validation, preview, button state
chat, notifications — data aata rehta hai, UI khud sync
pros: State desync bug practically khatam ho jaata hai
Component reusable hain — ek baar likho, 20 jagah use karo
Sabse bada ecosystem aur job market
cons: Sirf UI library hai — routing, data fetching sab alag se laana padta hai
Bundle size vanilla se zyada
Chhoti static site ke liye overkill

lessons.name: Setting up a React project — Vite, create-react-app, or Next.js
lessons.desc: Vite: npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react → fastest setup. CRA: npx create-react-app my-app → older, slower. Next.js: npx create-next-app@latest → for SSR/full-stack. For learning React basics, use Vite.
lessons.q: How do you create a new React project? What is the role of a bundler like Vite or Webpack?
lessons.qsub: What does a bundler actually do? Why do you need it — why can't you just write React in a .html file?
terms: tumhari 100 files ko browser ke liye chalne layak bana deta hai (Vite, webpack)
Hot Module Replacement — file save karte hi browser bina reload update ho jaata hai
React ke upar bana framework jisme routing/SSR built-in hai (Next.js)
lessons.what:
Definition: React project shuru karne ke 3 raste — Vite (fast, simple SPA), Next.js (routing + SSR + backend sab included), aur CRA (create-react-app — ab deprecated hai, use mat karo).

2026 mein: seekhne aur SPA ke liye Vite. Production website/product ke liye Next.js.
lessons.why: Browser import, JSX, TypeScript sidha nahi samajhta. Bundler in sabko plain JS mein badal ke ek file bana deta hai. Vite dev mein native ESM use karta hai isliye server 200ms mein start hota hai — CRA mein 30 second lagte the.
lessons.code:
# Vite -- seekhne ke liye best
npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts
cd my-app && npm install && npm run dev

# Next.js -- production app ke liye
npx create-next-app@latest my-app

# folder structure (Vite)
my-app/
  index.html        <- yahan se sab shuru hota hai
  src/
    main.tsx        <- React ko DOM se jodta hai
    App.tsx         <- tumhara root component
  vite.config.ts
  package.json
where: Next.js — SEO, routing, API sab chahiye
pros: Vite ka dev server almost instant hai
Next.js mein routing, image optimization, SSR free mein
Dono TypeScript out of the box support karte hain
cons: Next.js ka learning curve zyada hai (server vs client components)
Bahut saare config files initially confusing lagte hain
Ecosystem tez badalta hai — tutorials purane ho jaate hain
gotchas: create-react-app ab dead hai — koi bhi 2023 se purana tutorial CRA use karta ho to skip karo
Vite mein env variables VITE_ se shuru hone chahiye warna undefined milega
node_modules commit mat karo — .gitignore mein hona chahiye

lessons.name: Your first React component — Hello World
lessons.desc:
A React component is just a JavaScript function that returns JSX. function App() { return

Hello World

; } — that's a complete component. React renders it to the DOM via createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render().
lessons.q: What is a React component? How does React turn a component into actual HTML on the page?
lessons.qsub: What is the "root" element in index.html? How does React know where to mount your app?
terms: ek function jo UI (JSX) return karta hai
wo DOM element jisme poora React app render hota hai
component ko chalana taaki React ko pata chale screen pe kya dikhana hai
lessons.what:
Definition: React component ek normal JavaScript function hai jo JSX return karta hai. Ek hi niyam hai — naam capital letter se shuru hona chahiye.

function Button() = component. function button() = React isko HTML tag samjhega aur toot jaayega.
lessons.analogy: Lego block. Ek block banao (component), phir usse 50 jagah lagao. Har block ka apna shape hai aur wo doosre blocks ke saath fit ho jaata hai.
lessons.why: Component hi React ka reuse unit hai. Ek <Card> banao, 30 jagah use karo. Design badle to ek file badlo — 30 jagah badal jaayegi. Aur har component apne logic + markup + style ko ek saath rakhta hai, teen alag files mein nahi.
where: poora React isi ek cheez se bana hai
pros: Ek jagah likho, kahin bhi use karo
Markup + logic + style saath — dhoondhna aasan
Test karna aasan — bas function hai
cons: Bahut chhote components banane se files ka jungle ban jaata hai
Kab todna hai ye judgement seekhne mein time lagta hai
gotchas: Capital letter se naam shuru karo — warna React usko HTML tag samjhega
Component ek hi cheez return kar sakta hai — do siblings chahiye to <>...</> fragment use karo
return ke baad nayi line mein JSX shuru mat karo — JS automatic semicolon daal dega. () use karo

lessons.name: What is JSX? — HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript
lessons.desc:
JSX looks like HTML but it's actually JavaScript. Babel compiles

Hello

to React.createElement("h1", null, "Hello"). Rules: className instead of class, camelCase for attributes (onClick not onclick), all tags must close (
not
).
lessons.q: What is JSX? Is it valid JavaScript? How does it work under the hood?
lessons.qsub: Why does React use className instead of class? What happens if you use class instead?
terms: JavaScript ke andar HTML jaisa syntax likhne ka tarika
JSX ko normal JS function calls mein badalna (build time pe)
JSX ke andar { } jisme koi bhi JS expression daal sakte ho
lessons.what:
Definition: JSX JavaScript ka extension hai jo HTML jaisa dikhta hai. Browser isko nahi samajhta — build ke waqt ye React.createElement(...) calls mein badal jaata hai (React 17+ mein jsx()).

Matlab JSX syntax sugar hai — asli mein tum sirf function calls likh rahe ho.
lessons.analogy: Emoji. Tum 😀 dekhte ho, computer ke andar wo ek number (U+1F600) hai. Dikhne mein alag, andar se kuch aur.
lessons.why: Bina JSX ke nested UI likhna narak hai — 4 level nesting mein 4 nested createElement calls. JSX se wahi cheez HTML jaisi padhi jaati hai. Aur kyunki ye asli JS hai, tum map, ternary, variables sab seedha use kar sakte ho.

lessons.name: Props vs State — passing data and managing change
lessons.desc: Props: data passed FROM parent TO child — read-only, like function parameters. State: data that lives INSIDE a component — when it changes, React re-renders the component. Props are for "configuration", state is for "what changed". function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return <button onClick={() => setCount(c => c+1)}>{count}</button>; }
lessons.q: What is the difference between props and state in React?
lessons.qsub: What does it mean that props are immutable? What happens if you try to modify props directly?
terms: parent se child ko diya gaya data — child isse badal nahi sakta
component ka apna data jo badal sakta hai — badalne par re-render hota hai
component function ka dobara chalna taaki naya UI bane
lessons.what:
Definition: Do tarah ka data hota hai React mein:

  • Props — bahar se aaya (function ke arguments jaise). Read-only.
  • State — component ke andar ka, useState se banta hai. Badal sakta hai, aur badalne pe UI update hoti hai.

Ek line ka rule: badalta hai to state, nahi badalta to props.
lessons.analogy: Props = tumhara janm ka naam — parents ne diya, tum khud nahi badal sakte. State = tumhara mood — tumhara apna hai, badalta rehta hai, aur badalne par tumhara chehra bhi badal jaata hai.
lessons.why: Ye split "one-way data flow" banata hai — data hamesha upar se neeche behta hai. Isliye jab UI galat dikhe to tum upar chal ke source dhoondh sakte ho. Agar child parent ka data badal sakta to trace karna namumkin ho jaata.

lessons.name: JSX & React.createElement
lessons.desc: JSX is syntactic sugar — Babel compiles it to React.createElement() calls that return plain JS objects called React Elements.
lessons.q: What does JSX actually compile to? What is a React Element vs a React Component?
lessons.qsub: Why can't you return two sibling elements without a wrapper? What does Fragment solve?
terms: wo function jisme JSX transpile hota tha (classic runtime)
React 17+ ka naya tarika — jsx() function, import ki zaroorat nahi
JSX ka result — ek plain immutable object
lessons.what:
Definition: JSX compile hokar function call banta hai jo ek plain object return karta hai. Wo object hi "React Element" hai — ek description hai ki screen pe kya hona chahiye, koi asli DOM node nahi.

React 17 se pehle: React.createElement (isliye import React zaroori tha). React 17+ automatic runtime mein compiler khud jsx import kar leta hai.
lessons.why: Ye samajhna zaroori hai kyunki isse do baatein clear hoti hain: (1) JSX likhna sasta hai — sirf object banta hai, DOM ko haath nahi lagta; (2) <Foo /> Foo ko chalata nahi, sirf uska description banata hai. React decide karta hai kab chalana hai.
where: console.log(<X/>) karke element ka structure dekh sakte ho
element tree compare karne wale tools isi object pe kaam karte hain
Element vs Component vs Instance ka base yahi hai
pros: Element banana bahut sasta hai — koi DOM operation nahi
Immutable object hone se React safely compare kar sakta hai
React 17+ mein import React ki zaroorat khatam
cons: Ek extra abstraction layer samajhni padti hai
Purane tutorials classic runtime dikhate hain — confusion hoti hai
gotchas: <Foo /> likhne se Foo() call NAHI hota — sirf object banta hai
Element frozen hai — el.props.x = 1 chup-chaap fail ho jaayega
type string ho to DOM tag, function ho to component — yahi capital-letter rule ki wajah hai

lessons.name: Virtual DOM
lessons.desc: An in-memory JS object tree mirroring the real DOM — React diffs the new vs old tree and only applies minimal real DOM changes.
lessons.q: What is the Virtual DOM and why does React use it? Does it always make things faster?
lessons.qsub: What is the actual cost of the Virtual DOM? When would direct DOM manipulation be faster?
terms: asli DOM ka JS object mein banaya hua halka copy
purane aur naye tree ko compare karke farak nikalna
diff ke hisaab se asli DOM mein minimum changes karna
lessons.what: Definition: Virtual DOM asli DOM ka ek lightweight JavaScript representation hai. State badalne par React naya virtual tree banata hai, purane se compare karta hai, aur sirf jo badla hai utna hi asli DOM mein apply karta hai.
lessons.analogy: Ghar ka naksha. Deewar todne se pehle naksha banate ho, purane naksha se compare karte ho, aur sirf wahi deewar tod-te ho jo sach mein badalni hai. Poora ghar nahi girate.
lessons.why:
DOM operations mehnge hain — har change layout/paint trigger kar sakta hai. Agar React har state change pe poora DOM dobara banata to app rukk jaata. Diff JS objects pe hota hai (sasta), aur DOM pe sirf minimum update jaata hai (mehnga par kam).

Par sach ye hai — Virtual DOM manual optimized DOM code se tez nahi hai. Ye "kaafi tez" hai jabki tum declarative likh sakte ho. Speed nahi, DX (developer experience) iska point hai.

lessons.name: Class vs Functional Components
lessons.desc: Class components use lifecycle methods and this; functional components use hooks. Hooks give functions all the same capabilities — and more.
lessons.q: What are the key differences between class and functional components? Why did the React team move to hooks?
lessons.qsub: What does a class component have that functional components still cannot fully replicate?
terms: purana tarika — class extends React.Component, render() method
aaj ka standard — normal function + hooks
class ke special methods — componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate...
lessons.what:
Definition: React mein component do tarah se likhe jaate the. Class (2019 se pehle) mein this.state, this.setState, aur lifecycle methods the. Functional (aaj) mein hooks se wahi cheezein hoti hain, bina this ke.

Aaj naya code hamesha functional hota hai. Class sirf legacy code aur Error Boundaries mein milti hai.
lessons.why: Class mein ek hi kaam ka logic 3 lifecycle methods mein bat jaata tha (subscribe componentDidMount mein, update componentDidUpdate mein, cleanup componentWillUnmount mein). lessons.name: Props & Immutability
lessons.desc: Props are read-only inputs flowing parent → child. Mutating props directly breaks the one-way data flow contract.
lessons.q: Why are props immutable? What happens to child components when a parent re-renders?
lessons.qsub: What is prop drilling and what are the solutions? When is prop drilling actually fine?
terms: special prop — tag ke andar likha hua content
{...obj} se saare props ek saath pass karna
lessons.what: Definition: Props parent se child ko diya gaya data hai. React inhe read-only treat karta hai — child props ko badal nahi sakta. React ka rule: "har component apne props ke maamle mein pure function ki tarah behave kare".
lessons.why: Immutability isliye zaroori hai kyunki React reference compare karta hai (Object.is). Agar tumne object ko andar se badal diya, reference wahi rahega, React ko lagega kuch nahi badla, aur UI update hi nahi hogi. Isliye hamesha naya object/array banao.
where: data neeche pass karne ka standard tarika
children se flexible wrapper bante hain
pros: Component predictable — same props, same UI
Reference comparison se React fast diff kar paata hai
children se composition bahut flexible ho jaati hai
cons: Har update pe naya object — thoda garbage banta hai
Deep nested update ke liye spread chain lambi ho jaati hai
Prop drilling deep tree mein dard deti hai
gotchas: sort(), reverse(), splice(), push() sab ORIGINAL badalte hain — pehle copy banao
Inline object/array prop ({} ya []) har render naya reference banata hai — memo tod deta hai
Spread se pehle apne props likho warna user override nahi kar payega

lessons.name: State & Re-renders
lessons.desc: State is private, mutable data that when changed schedules a re-render. React batches state updates for efficiency.
lessons.q: What triggers a re-render in React? What does NOT trigger a re-render?
lessons.qsub: If you call setState with the same value as current state, does React re-render?
terms: hook jo state banata hai — [value, setValue] deta hai
kai setState ek saath milaakar ek hi re-render karna
setX(prev => ...) — purani value se nayi banana
lessons.what:
Definition: State component ka apna data hai jo re-render ke beech yaad rehta hai aur jise badalne par React re-render karta hai. const [x, setX] = useState(initial).

Do zaroori sach: (1) setX turant value nahi badalta — agli render mein nayi value milti hai; (2) React ek event ke saare setState batch karke ek hi re-render karta hai.
lessons.analogy: Photo. Har render ek photo hai jisme us waqt ki value freeze hai. setX naye photo ka order deta hai — par tumhare haath mein abhi bhi purani photo hai.
lessons.why: Ye samajhe bina sabse classic bug aata hai — setCount(count+1) teen baar likho to +3 nahi, +1 hota hai. Kyunki teeno mein count ek hi purani photo se aa raha hai. Functional update setCount(c => c+1) mein React latest value deta hai, isliye +3 hota hai.

Lazy init se mehnga initial calculation sirf ek baar

Object/array state manually copy karni padti hai
Bahut saare related useState ho jaayein to useReducer better hai

Jo purani value pe depend kare wo hamesha functional update se karo

lessons.name: Keys in Lists
lessons.desc: Keys help React identify which items in a list changed, were added, or removed — critical for correct reconciliation.
lessons.q: Why does React need keys? What happens if you use index as a key? When is index as key actually safe?
lessons.qsub: What is key remounting? When would you deliberately change a key to reset a component?
terms: list ke har item ko di gayi unique pehchan
array ka position (0,1,2) key ki tarah use karna — aksar galat
component ka poora naya banna — saara internal state khatam
lessons.what: Definition: Key ek special prop hai jo React ko batata hai ki list ke do render ke beech kaunsa item wahi item hai. Bina key ke React position se match karta hai, jo item add/remove/reorder hone par galat ho jaata hai.
lessons.analogy: Class mein roll number. Agar bacche ko position se pehchano (pehla, doosra) aur ek bacha beech se chala jaaye, to sabki pehchan shift ho jaayegi. Roll number (key) se aisa nahi hoga.
lessons.why: Ye sirf warning chupane ki baat nahi — asli bug hota hai. List ke beech mein item add karo, index key ke saath: React position 0 pe naya item dekhta hai, sochta hai "wahi purana item hai bas text badal gaya", to DOM node reuse kar leta hai. Result — input mein typed text galat row mein chala jaata hai, checkbox galat item pe tick reh jaata hai.

Reorder pe React nodes move karta hai, dobara banata nahi
key badal ke reset karna ek clean trick hai
cons: Stable id nahi ho to key banana mushkil hota hai
Math.random() key har render remount kar degi — bahut slow
Galat key ka bug bahut confusing dikhta hai
gotchas: key sirf sibling ke beech unique honi chahiye, globally nahi
key ko props se padh nahi sakte — props.key undefined hai, React use khud rakh leta hai

lessons.name: Controlled vs Uncontrolled Components
lessons.desc: Controlled: React state owns the input value. Uncontrolled: the DOM owns it via refs. Both have legitimate use cases.
lessons.q: What is the difference between controlled and uncontrolled inputs? When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: What is the problem with defaultValue vs value in React inputs?
terms: input ki value React state se aati hai
input apni value khud DOM mein rakhta hai, React sirf ref se padhta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Do tarah ke form inputs:

  • Controlled — value={state} + onChange. React ke paas har waqt sach hai.
  • Uncontrolled — defaultValue + ref. DOM ke paas sach hai, React sirf submit pe padhta hai.
lessons.analogy: Controlled = har shabd bolne se pehle manager se poochna. Uncontrolled = kaam khud karo, meeting mein report do.
lessons.why: Controlled isliye default hai kyunki tumhe har keystroke pe control milta hai — live validation, character counter, input formatting (phone number mein dash), doosre field ko disable karna. Uncontrolled fast hai (koi re-render nahi) par ye sab nahi kar sakte.
where: hamesha uncontrolled — security ki wajah se
React Hook Form uncontrolled use karta hai — isliye fast hai
pros: Controlled: poora control, live validation, formatting, dependent fields
Uncontrolled: har keystroke pe re-render nahi — bade form mein tez
React Hook Form dono ka best mila deta hai
cons: Controlled: 30 fields ka form har keystroke pe re-render — slow
Uncontrolled: value React state mein nahi, dependent logic mushkil
Dono mix karne par confusing bugs
gotchas: value diya aur onChange nahi diya to input type hi nahi hoga — readOnly ya defaultValue use karo
value undefined se string ho jaaye to warning: "changing uncontrolled to controlled" — initial value hamesha "" rakho
File input controlled ho hi nahi sakta — browser security

lessons.name: StrictMode
lessons.desc: A development-only tool that double-invokes render/lifecycle functions to surface side effect bugs and deprecated API usage.
lessons.q: What does StrictMode do? Why does it call some functions twice in development?
lessons.qsub: If StrictMode causes bugs by double-invoking effects, what does that reveal about your code?
terms: ek wrapper component jo dev mein extra checks karta hai
dev mein render aur effect ko jaan-boojh ke do baar chalana
do baar chalane par bhi wahi natija — koi extra side effect nahi
lessons.what:
Definition: <StrictMode> ek dev-only wrapper hai. Ye kuch render nahi karta — bas React se kehta hai "extra sakhti se check karo". Sabse dikhne wala effect: components do baar render hote hain aur effects do baar chalte hain (mount → unmount → mount).

Production build mein ye bilkul kuch nahi karta.
lessons.analogy: Fire drill. Aag lagi nahi hai, par jaan-boojh ke alarm bajate hain ye dekhne ke liye ki nikalne ka rasta sach mein kaam karta hai ya nahi.
lessons.why:
React 18+ mein future features (Offscreen, Suspense ke saath state preserve karna) component ko unmount karke wapas mount kar sakti hain. Agar tumhara effect cleanup galat hai — timer clear nahi kiya, subscription band nahi kiya — to wo tab bura crash karega. StrictMode aaj hi wo bug dikha deta hai.

Do baar API call dikhna bug nahi hai — wo StrictMode hai. Usse "fix" karne ke liye ref-guard mat lagao; asli fix cleanup mein abort karna hai.
where: har naye project mein by default hota hai
cleanup sahi hai ya nahi turant pata chalta hai
pros: Missing cleanup aur impure render turant pakadta hai
Production mein zero cost
Deprecated API ki warning deta hai
cons: Do baar log/network dekh ke beginners bahut confuse hote hain
Kuch purani libraries StrictMode mein tootti hain
Console noise badh jaata hai
gotchas: Do baar chalna DEV-ONLY hai — production mein ek hi baar chalega
StrictMode hataake "fix" mat karo — wo bug chhupana hai, hatana nahi
Render function pure honi chahiye — usme koi mutation ya side effect mat karo

lessons.name: React Fiber Architecture
lessons.desc: The complete rewrite of React's reconciler (React 16+). Fiber turns the render tree into a linked list of units of work that can be paused, aborted, and resumed.
lessons.q: What is React Fiber and why was it a complete rewrite? What problem does it solve over the old stack reconciler?
lessons.qsub: What is a Fiber node? What properties does it hold?
terms: ek JS object jo ek component ke kaam ko represent karta hai
purana React (v15) — recursion se chalta tha, rok nahi sakte the
kaam beech mein rok ke baad mein resume kar sakna
lessons.what:
Definition: Fiber React 16+ ka reconciliation engine hai. Har component ke liye ek fiber node banta hai — ek plain object jisme us component ka type, props, state, aur uske parent/child/sibling ke pointers hote hain.

Isse recursion linked-list traversal ban jaata hai, aur linked list ko tum beech mein rok sakte ho. Yahi Fiber ka poora point hai.
lessons.analogy: Kitaab padhna. Recursion = ek saans mein poori kitaab padhna, koi roke to shuru se. Fiber = bookmark lagana — jahan ruke wahin se aage.
lessons.why:
React 15 mein reconciliation recursive tha. Recursion JS call stack use karta hai aur call stack ko beech mein pause nahi kiya jaa sakta. 5000 components ka tree = 200ms tak main thread block = user ka typing freeze.

Fiber mein React har node ke baad pooch sakta hai "kya browser ko koi urgent kaam hai?" Agar haan to ruk jaata hai, browser ko chalne deta hai, phir wahin se resume karta hai. Isi ki wajah se useTransition, Suspense, aur concurrent rendering possible hue.

lessons.name: Reconciliation & Diffing Algorithm
lessons.desc: React's O(n) algorithm for comparing two trees using two heuristics: elements of different types produce different trees; keys identify stable elements across renders.
lessons.q: Explain how React's diffing algorithm works. What are its two key assumptions that make it O(n) instead of O(n³)?
lessons.qsub: What happens in the diff when a parent changes from a <div> to a <span>? What about when you reorder list items with vs without keys?
terms: purane aur naye tree ko compare karke DOM changes nikalna
shortcut rule jo hamesha perfect nahi par practically sahi hota hai
n items ke liye n steps — linear, fast
lessons.what:
Definition: Reconciliation wo algorithm hai jo purane fiber tree ko naye element tree se compare karta hai. Perfect tree-diff O(n³) hota hai — 1000 nodes ke liye ek arab operations. React do heuristics lagakar isko O(n) bana deta hai:

  1. Alag type = alag tree. Compare hi mat karo, poora hataake naya banao.
  2. Same level pe items ko key se match karo.
lessons.why:
Ye do rules practically hamesha sach hote hain — log <div> ko <span> mein badal ke usi content ki ummeed nahi karte. Iske badle React 1000x fast ho jaata hai.

Par iska ek bada side effect hai: type badalne par subtree ka poora state chala jaata hai. Ye "mera input reset kyun ho gaya" bug ki asli wajah hoti hai.

lessons.name: Render Phase vs Commit Phase
lessons.desc: Render phase: pure, interruptible work — React builds the new Fiber tree. Commit phase: synchronous, non-interruptible — React applies DOM mutations and runs effects.
lessons.q: What is the difference between the render phase and commit phase? Why must the render phase be pure?
lessons.qsub: In which phase do useEffect and useLayoutEffect run? Why does useLayoutEffect need to be synchronous?
terms: React soch raha hai kya badla — pure, interruptible
React DOM ko sach mein badal raha hai — synchronous, uninterruptible
un fibers ki list jinme kuch DOM kaam karna hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Har update do phases mein hota hai:

  • Render (soch) — component functions chalte hain, naya tree banta hai, diff hota hai. Koi DOM change nahi. Ye ruk sakta hai, dobara chal sakta hai, cancel ho sakta hai.
  • Commit (kaam) — DOM update, refs set, effects chalao. Ye ek saath, bina ruke hota hai.
lessons.analogy: Ghar ka naksha banana (render) vs deewar khadi karna (commit). Naksha 10 baar phaad ke naya bana sakte ho — kuch nuksaan nahi. Deewar khadi kar di to beech mein rok nahi sakte.
lessons.why:
Ye split hi sab kuch samjhata hai:

  • Render phase mein side effect mat karo — kyunki wo do baar chal sakta hai ya cancel ho sakta hai (StrictMode isi liye double-invoke karta hai).
  • useEffect commit ke baad chalta hai (browser paint ke baad) — isliye async lagta hai.
  • useLayoutEffect commit ke andar, paint se pehle chalta hai — isliye DOM measure karne ke liye sahi hai par blocking hai.

lessons.name: React Scheduler & Priority Lanes
lessons.desc: React's scheduler assigns priority lanes to updates (SyncLane, InputContinuousLane, DefaultLane, IdleLane) and processes high-priority work first.
lessons.q: How does React prioritize which updates to process first? What are lanes in React?
lessons.qsub: How does startTransition use the scheduler to deprioritize an update?
terms: React ka apna module jo decide karta hai kaunsa kaam kab chale
priority ka ek bit — React 18 mein 31 lanes hain
low-priority kaam ka kabhi chance na milna
lessons.what:
Definition: Scheduler React ka priority system hai. Har update ko ek lane milti hai. Zyada urgent lane pehle process hoti hai; kam urgent kaam ruk ke wait karta hai.

Priority order (upar sabse urgent): Sync (discrete events jaise click/input) → InputContinuous (hover, drag) → Default (normal setState) → Transition (startTransition) → Idle (offscreen).
lessons.analogy: Hospital emergency ward. Heart attack (click) pehle, fracture (hover) uske baad, routine checkup (transition) intezaar karega. Par routine wale ko bhi kabhi na kabhi number aa hi jaata hai (starvation se bachav).
lessons.why: Bina priority ke sab kaam barabar hai — bade list ka filter typing ko block kar dega. Lanes ki wajah se React keh sakta hai "typing pehle, filtered list baad mein", aur filter ka kaam beech mein interrupt karke typing dikha deta hai. useTransition exactly yahi karta hai.
where: bhaari tab ko transition mein daalo
pros: Urgent updates kabhi block nahi hote
Bitmask se priority check almost free hai
Starvation se bachav built-in hai
cons: Andar se samajhna mushkil
Galat priority di to UI aur laggy lag sakti hai
requestIdleCallback se pehle React ne apna scheduler likha — extra code
gotchas: Sab kuch transition mein daalne se sab kuch dheema ho jaayega — sirf bhaari kaam
startTransition ke andar async await ke baad ka code transition mein NAHI hota
Scheduler npm pe alag package hai — React ka hissa par independent

lessons.name: Work Loop & Time Slicing
lessons.desc: The Fiber work loop processes one Fiber node at a time, yielding back to the browser every ~5ms so frames aren't blocked — enabling interruptible rendering.
lessons.q: What is time slicing in React? How does the work loop enable rendering without blocking the browser?
lessons.qsub: What API does React use to yield back to the browser (MessageChannel, requestIdleCallback, etc.) and why?
terms: wo loop jo ek-ek fiber process karta hai
kaam ko 5ms ke tukdon mein baant ke chalana
main thread browser ko wapas de dena
lessons.what: Definition: Work loop React ka main engine hai. Ye ek while loop hai jo ek-ek fiber pe kaam karta hai, aur har fiber ke baad poochta hai — "kya mera 5ms ka time khatam ho gaya?" Agar haan, to yield karta hai (browser ko chalne deta hai) aur agle frame mein wahin se resume karta hai.
lessons.analogy: Padhai karte waqt har 25 minute pe break (Pomodoro). Kaam poora hota hai, par tum machine nahi ban-te — beech mein zaroori cheezein ho jaati hain.
lessons.why: Browser ek frame 16.6ms mein banata hai (60fps). Agar React 200ms tak thread pakde rahe to 12 frames drop ho jaayenge — user ko lagega app hang ho gaya. 5ms slices se React kaam karta rehta hai aur browser bhi paint karta rehta hai. Kaam ka total time same rehta hai, par app responsive lagta hai.

lessons.name: Batching (React 17 vs React 18)
lessons.desc: React 17 only batches state updates inside React event handlers. React 18 batches ALL updates — including setTimeout, promises, and native events — automatically.
lessons.q: What is state batching? How does React 18's automatic batching differ from React 17? How do you opt out?
lessons.qsub: What is flushSync and when would you need it?
terms: kai state updates ko milaakar ek hi re-render karna
React 18 ka feature — har jagah batching, sirf event handler mein nahi
batching ko force tod ke turant render karana
lessons.what:
Definition: Batching yaani ek hi tick mein hue saare setState ko jodkar sirf ek re-render karna.

React 17 mein batching sirf React event handlers mein hoti thi. setTimeout, promise, ya native listener ke andar har setState alag render karta tha. React 18 mein har jagah batching hoti hai — isi ko "automatic batching" kehte hain.
lessons.why: 3 setState = 3 render matlab 3 baar poora tree diff + 3 DOM commits. Batch karne se 1 render. React 17 mein fetch().then(() => { setLoading(false); setData(d); }) do render karta tha — beech mein ek frame aisa hota tha jahan loading false hai par data abhi nahi aaya (flash of empty state). React 18 mein ye bug apne aap khatam ho gaya.

lessons.name: React Element vs Component vs Instance
lessons.desc: Element: a plain object describing what to render. Component: a function/class that returns elements. Instance: only class components have instances (this).
lessons.q: What is the difference between a React element, a React component, and a React instance?
lessons.qsub: Why don't functional components have instances? What does that mean for refs?
terms: plain immutable object — "kya dikhna chahiye" ka description
function ya class — jo element banata hai
fiber node — chalte hue component ka asli record (state, effects)
lessons.what:
Definition: Teen alag cheezein jo log mila dete hain:

  • Component = recipe (function Card)
  • Element = order slip (<Card title="Hi"/> — ek object, abhi kuch chala nahi)
  • Instance = asli dish (fiber node jisme state, effects, DOM pointer hai)
lessons.analogy: Recipe (component) → order slip (element) → plate mein bani dish (instance). Ek recipe se 100 order slip, har order slip se ek alag dish.
lessons.why:
Ye farak samajhne se do sawaal apne aap clear ho jaate hain:

  • "Element banane se component chalta hai?" Nahi. <Card/> sirf object banata hai. React decide karta hai kab Card() call karna hai.
  • "State kahan rehta hai?" Component mein nahi (wo to sirf function hai), element mein nahi (wo immutable hai) — instance/fiber mein. Isiliye fiber destroy hote hi state chala jaata hai.

lessons.name: Rules of Hooks & Their Internals
lessons.desc: Hooks must be called at top level and only from React functions. React stores hook state in a linked list on the Fiber node, indexed by call order.
lessons.q: Why can't hooks be called inside conditionals or loops? What would break internally if you did?
lessons.qsub: How does React know which useState call corresponds to which state value across re-renders?
terms: use se shuru hone wala special function jo React feature deta hai
jis order mein hooks call hote hain — React isi se unhe pehchanta hai
ek ke baad ek jude hue nodes — React hooks isi mein store karta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Do rules:

  1. Hooks sirf top level pe call karo — if, loop, ya nested function ke andar nahi.
  2. Sirf React function component ya custom hook ke andar call karo.

Wajah ek line mein: React hooks ko naam se nahi, order se pehchanta hai.
lessons.analogy: Line mein khade log bina naam ke. Ginti karke pata chalta hai kaun kaun hai — "pehla, doosra, teesra". Agar doosra aadmi kabhi kabhi line mein na aaye, to teesra galti se doosra ban jaayega.
lessons.why: Fiber ke andar hooks ek linked list mein hain. Har render pe React list ko shuru se chalta hai — pehla useState call → pehla node, doosra call → doosra node. Agar tumne if ke andar hook rakha aur condition false ho gayi, to poori list shift ho jaayegi — name ki jagah age ka state mil jaayega. React isko detect nahi kar sakta, isliye lint rule hai.

Early return se pehle sab hooks likhne padte hain

lessons.name: useState Internals
lessons.desc: useState stores its value in a hook queue on the Fiber node. The setter enqueues an update and triggers a re-render. Functional updates avoid stale closure problems.
lessons.q: How does useState work under the hood? What is the difference between setState(value) and setState(prev => value)?
lessons.qsub: What is a stale closure in the context of useState? Write a code example that demonstrates the bug and fix it.
terms: fiber ke andar ek object jisme us hook ka state hai
value same hai to React render skip kar deta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: useState fiber ke memoizedState linked list mein ek node banata hai. Us node mein hoti hai — current value, aur ek update queue jisme pending setState pade rehte hain.

Render ke waqt React queue ke saare updates ek-ek karke apply karta hai aur final value nikalta hai.
lessons.why:
Andar dekhne se do practical cheezein samajh aati hain:

  • Functional update kyun kaam karta hai — queue mein tumhara function pada hai, aur React use us waqt ki latest value deta hai, purani snapshot nahi.
  • Same value set karne se render kyun nahi hota — React Object.is se compare karke bail out kar deta hai. Par pehla render fir bhi ho sakta hai (React ek baar check karta hai).

samajhna kyun state purana dikh raha hai
"useState andar se kaise kaam karta hai"
pros: API bahut simple hai
Bailout se bewajah render nahi hota
Functional update se concurrency safe
cons: Order dependency ki wajah se conditional use nahi kar sakte
Object state manually copy karni padti hai
Bahut saare related states ho to sync rakhna mushkil
gotchas: setState bailout hone par bhi React kabhi kabhi ek extra render karta hai — ye normal hai
useState(fn) mein React fn ko INITIALIZER samjhega — function state chahiye to useState(() => fn)
Do useState ko ek object mein jodna aksar behtar hota hai jab wo saath badalte hain

lessons.name: useEffect — Timing, Deps, Cleanup
lessons.desc: Runs after paint, asynchronously. The dependency array controls when it re-runs. The cleanup function runs before the next effect or on unmount.
lessons.q: Explain useEffect's full lifecycle: when does it run, when does cleanup run, what is the dependency array contract?
lessons.qsub: What happens if you put a function in the dependency array? How do you fix the infinite loop?
terms: render ke bahar ka kaam — fetch, timer, subscription, DOM
wo values jinke badalne par effect dobara chale
effect ka return kiya hua function — agle effect se pehle chalta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: useEffect(fn, deps) React ko kehta hai "commit + paint ke baad ye kaam karo". deps array batati hai kab dobara chalana hai.

  • Koi array nahi → har render
  • [] → sirf mount pe (aur StrictMode dev mein 2 baar)
  • [a, b] → jab a ya b badle

Cleanup har baar chalta hai effect dobara chalne se pehle — sirf unmount pe nahi.
lessons.analogy: Kamre se nikalte waqt light band karna. Har baar nikalte ho to band karte ho — sirf ghar chhodte waqt nahi.
lessons.why:
Cleanup ka har-baar chalna hi race condition se bachata hai. Tum tez-tez user badlo — 3 fetch chal padte hain. Bina cleanup ke jo sabse late aayega wo jeetega, chahe wo purana user ho. Cleanup mein abort karne se sirf latest request survive karti hai.

React 18 ka guidance: useEffect data fetching ke liye ideal nahi hai. React Query ya framework loader use karo — wo caching, dedup, retry sab handle karte hain.

Deps se automatic re-sync
Custom hooks mein aasani se wrap ho jaata hai
cons: Data fetching ke liye ye galat tool hai — waterfall aur race conditions
Deps galat hone se infinite loop ya stale data
Object/function deps har render badalte hain
gotchas: Jo cheez render ke waqt calculate ho sakti hai uske liye effect + state MAT banao
Object/function ko dep mat banao — primitive nikalo ya useMemo/useCallback karo
eslint exhaustive-deps warning ko chup mat karo — usko samjho, aksar wo sahi hoti hai

lessons.name: useLayoutEffect vs useEffect
lessons.desc: useLayoutEffect fires synchronously after DOM mutations but before paint — identical to componentDidMount/Update. useEffect fires after paint.
lessons.q: When would you use useLayoutEffect over useEffect? Give a concrete real-world example.
lessons.qsub: Why does React warn against useLayoutEffect in SSR? How do you work around it?
terms: browser ka screen pe pixels banana
baar baar DOM measure karke badalna — bahut slow
user ko ek frame ke liye galat UI dikhna
lessons.what:
Definition: Dono commit ke baad chalte hain, par timing alag:

  • useLayoutEffect — DOM update ke baad, paint se PEHLE. Synchronous, browser ko rok deta hai.
  • useEffect — paint ke BAAD. Async, browser ko nahi rokta.

Default hamesha useEffect. useLayoutEffect sirf jab DOM measure karke usi frame mein badalna ho.
lessons.analogy: Photo kheenchne se pehle baal theek karna (useLayoutEffect) vs photo aane ke baad theek karna (useEffect). Doosre case mein pehli photo mein baal kharab dikhenge.
lessons.why: Tooltip ka classic case: pehle render mein tooltip (0,0) pe hai. useEffect se position set karoge to user ko ek frame ke liye tooltip corner mein dikhega phir jump karega — flicker. useLayoutEffect mein position paint se pehle set ho jaati hai, user ko kabhi galat jagah dikhta hi nahi.

DOM measurement guaranteed sahi milta hai
Layout ke saath sync rehta hai
cons: Blocking hai — bhaari kaam poore app ko atkaa dega

Overuse se performance kharab
gotchas: Default useEffect hi rakho — layout effect sirf measure-then-mutate ke liye

lessons.name: useRef — Beyond DOM Access
lessons.desc: useRef returns a stable object { current } that persists across renders without triggering re-renders. Use it for: DOM access, timers, previous values, and mutable instance variables.
lessons.q: What are the three main uses of useRef? How is it different from useState for storing values?
lessons.qsub: How do you implement a usePrevious hook? Why does it work?
terms: wo value jo renders ke beech bachi rahe par render trigger na kare
lessons.what:
Definition: useRef(init) ek object { current: init } deta hai jo poore component ke jeevan bhar wahi object rehta hai. .current badalne se re-render nahi hota.

Do kaam: (1) DOM node pakadna, (2) aisi value rakhna jo yaad rahe par UI se lena-dena na ho (timer id, previous value, flag).
lessons.analogy: Jeb. Kuch bhi rakh lo, nikal lo — kisi ko batana nahi padta (koi re-render nahi). State ek notice board hai — kuch badla to sab dekhte hain.
lessons.why: Kabhi kabhi value yaad rakhni hoti hai par UI usse nahi banti — interval ka id, "pehli render hai kya" flag, previous props. Agar isko state banaoge to har badlav pe bewajah render hoga. Ref exactly ye gap bharta hai.

Poore lifetime ek hi object — reference stable

Overuse karo to code imperative aur untraceable ho jaata hai
Ref badalne pe UI update nahi hoti — bhool jaao to bug

lessons.name: useMemo — When to Use & When Not To
lessons.desc: Memoizes the result of an expensive computation. Only recalculates when dependencies change. Costs memory and code complexity — only worth it for genuinely expensive work.
lessons.q: When should you use useMemo? What is the overhead of useMemo itself? When does it hurt performance?
lessons.qsub: Prove that useMemo is not a semantic guarantee — React can choose to discard memoized values. Does that matter?
terms: result yaad rakhna taaki dobara calculate na karna pade
har render pe wahi object reference milna
bina napay optimize karna — aksar nuksaan
lessons.what:
Definition: useMemo(fn, deps) calculation ka result yaad rakhta hai. Deps na badle to fn dobara nahi chalta — purana result milta hai.

Do jaayaz wajah: (1) sach mein mehnga calculation, (2) reference stable rakhna taaki neeche wala memo/effect na toote.
lessons.why:
Doosri wajah zyada important hai. const opts = {a:1} har render naya object banata hai. Agar wo React.memo wale child ko props mein ja raha hai, to memo bekaar ho gaya — child har baar re-render hoga. useMemo se reference stable rehta hai.

Par har cheez memo mat karo. useMemo ki apni cost hai — deps compare, memory. Ek simple a+b ko memo karna nuksaan hai. React 19 ka compiler ye kaam apne aap karne laga hai.
where: provider ka value hamesha memo karo
pros: Sach mein bhaari calculation bach jaata hai
Reference stability se neeche ka memo chain bacha rehta hai
Effect ke infinite loop rok deta hai
cons: Khud ki cost hai — memory + deps comparison
Deps galat to stale value ka silent bug
Code padhne mein bhaari ho jaata hai
gotchas: Pehle Profiler se naapo, phir memo karo — andaaze se mat karo
useMemo guarantee nahi hai — React memory pressure mein cache phenk sakta hai
Har render pe naya object/array props mein jaa raha ho tabhi memo ka sach mein fayda hai

lessons.name: useCallback — Referential Stability
lessons.desc: Returns a memoized function reference that only changes when dependencies change. Critical when passing callbacks to memoized child components.
lessons.q: Why does useCallback exist? When does it actually help performance vs when is it wasted?
lessons.qsub: If useCallback is just useMemo returning a function, when would you choose one over the other?
terms: function ka reference stable rakhta hai
do function same hain ya nahi — content nahi, address compare hota hai
lessons.what:
Definition: useCallback(fn, deps) = useMemo(() => fn, deps). Ye function ko yaad rakhta hai taaki har render pe wahi reference mile.

JavaScript mein har render pe () => {} ek naya function object hai — dikhne mein same, reference alag. Isi wajah se child ka React.memo toot jaata hai.
lessons.why:
useCallback akela bekaar hai. Uska fayda tabhi hai jab receiver reference care karta ho — yaani child React.memo mein ho, ya function kisi effect ki dep ho, ya custom hook ke andar jaa raha ho.

Agar child memo mein nahi hai to useCallback lagane se sirf cost badhi, fayda zero.

Effect infinite loop rukta hai
Custom hook consumers ke liye predictable
cons: Akela kuch nahi karta — memo ke bina bekaar

Har handler pe lagane se code bhaari
gotchas: React.memo ke bina useCallback ka koi fayda nahi — dono chahiye
Khali deps [] mein purana state capture ho jaata hai — functional update use karo

lessons.name: useReducer — Complex State Logic
lessons.desc: An alternative to useState for complex state transitions. Takes (state, action) => newState. Makes state logic testable and colocated.
lessons.q: When would you choose useReducer over useState? Implement a cart with useReducer.
lessons.qsub: How does useReducer + useContext compare to Redux? When would you still reach for Redux?
terms: ek object jo batata hai kya hua — { type: "...", payload }
lessons.what:
Definition: useReducer(reducer, initial) — jab kai state values ek doosre se jude hon, unhe alag alag useState mein rakhne ki jagah ek reducer mein rakho. Har badlav ek "action" hai.

Rule of thumb: 3+ related states ya ek event kai states badalta ho → useReducer.
lessons.analogy: Bank. Tum khud balance nahi badalte — "1000 nikalo" ka form (action) bharte ho. Bank rules (reducer) check karke naya balance banata hai. Har transaction ka record rehta hai.
lessons.why:
4 alag useState ke saath "loading true, error null, data null" har jagah manually likhna padta hai — ek jagah bhool gaye to impossible state ban jaata hai (loading true aur error dono). Reducer mein wo transition ek jagah likhi hai, isliye galat combination ban hi nahi sakta.

Bonus: dispatch ka reference hamesha stable hai — usse dep array mein daalna safe hai.
pros: Saari transitions ek jagah — padhna aur test karna aasan
Discriminated union se impossible states hi nahi ban-te
dispatch stable hai — dep array safe
cons: Chhote state ke liye zyada boilerplate
Action types define karne padte hain
Indirection — logic component se door chala jaata hai
gotchas: Reducer PURE honi chahiye — usme fetch/timer/mutation kuch nahi
dispatch stable hai, isliye use dep array ya context mein safely daal sakte ho
useState mein bhi reducer chhupa hai — useState useReducer ka special case hai

lessons.name: useContext — Performance Trap
lessons.desc: Subscribes a component to the nearest context value. Every context value change re-renders ALL consumers — even if they only use part of the value.
lessons.q: What is the performance problem with useContext? How do you prevent unnecessary re-renders from context changes?
lessons.qsub: What are the patterns to split context to avoid over-rendering? How does Zustand solve this differently?
terms: tree ke neeche data pahunchane ka rasta bina props ke
wo component jo value deta hai
wo component jo useContext se value leta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Context prop drilling se bachne ka tarika hai. Provider ek value deta hai, aur tree ke andar kahin bhi useContext se wo value mil jaati hai.

Performance trap: jab context ka value badalta hai to saare consumers re-render hote hain — chahe unhone us value ka sirf ek chhota hissa use kiya ho.
lessons.analogy: Ghar ka WiFi. Har kamre mein taar nahi bichhani padti (prop drilling). Par WiFi ka password badlo to sabhi devices disconnect ho jaate hain — chahe kisi ko sirf printer chahiye tha.
lessons.why:
Sabse aam bug: <Ctx.Provider value={{ user, setUser }}>. Ye object har render pe naya hai, isliye har parent render pe saare consumers re-render honge — chahe user badla hi na ho. Fix: value ko useMemo karo.

Doosra fix: context ko tod do — badalne wala data alag context, na badalne wala (functions) alag. Tab jo sirf functions use karta hai wo data badalne pe render nahi hoga.

pros: Prop drilling khatam
Provider swap karke test karna aasan
Built-in — koi library nahi chahiye

Selector nahi hai — value ka ek hissa subscribe nahi kar sakte
Tez badalne wale data ke liye bilkul galat (Zustand/Jotai better)

Context ko state manager mat samjho — wo dependency injection ka tool hai
Tez badalne wala data (mouse position, form values) context mein mat daalo

lessons.name: Custom Hooks — Architecture Pattern
lessons.desc: Functions starting with "use" that call other hooks — encapsulate and reuse stateful logic without changing component hierarchy.
lessons.q: What is a custom hook? How does it differ from a utility function? When should you extract one?
lessons.qsub: Build useFetch, useLocalStorage, and useDebounce custom hooks. What are their edge cases?
terms: use se shuru hone wala function jo doosre hooks use karta hai
wo logic jisme state ya effect ho
chhote hooks ko jodkar bada banana
lessons.what:
Definition: Custom hook ek normal function hai jo (a) use se shuru hota hai aur (b) andar doosre hooks call karta hai. Isse tum stateful logic ko component se alag karke reuse kar sakte ho.

Important: har component ko apni alag copy milti hai. Custom hook state share nahi karta — logic share karta hai.
lessons.analogy: Recipe. Do log same recipe se biryani banayein to biryani do alag degchi mein banegi — recipe share hui, khana nahi.
lessons.why: Class ke zamane mein logic reuse ke liye HOC aur render props the, jo "wrapper hell" bana dete the — DevTools mein 8 layer nesting. Custom hooks flat hain: const {data} = useUser(id). Koi extra component nahi, koi nesting nahi.
pros: Wrapper hell khatam — DevTools tree saaf
Test karna aasan (renderHook se)
Chhote hooks jodkar bade banaye jaa sakte hain
cons: State share nahi hoti — har call apni copy
Sirf function components mein
Bahut zyada hooks banane se indirection badhta hai
gotchas: Custom hook state SHARE nahi karta — uske liye Context ya store chahiye
Naam use se shuru karo warna lint rules apply nahi honge
Return kiye functions ko useCallback karo, objects ko useMemo — consumer ke liye stable

lessons.name: State Architecture — What Lives Where
lessons.desc: Local state → component. Shared UI state → lift up or context. Server state → React Query/SWR. Global app state → Zustand/Redux.
lessons.q: How do you decide where state should live? Walk me through your decision framework for a real app.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between server state and client state? Why does that distinction matter?
terms: data jo server ka hai — tumhare paas uski copy hai (users, posts)
data jo sirf tumhare browser ka hai (modal open, form draft)
jo doosre data se calculate ho sakta hai — state hona hi nahi chahiye
lessons.what:
Definition: State ko jagah dena ek decision hai, default nahi. Sabse zaroori sawaal — ye server ka data hai ya client ka?

  • Server state → React Query / SWR / framework loader. useState mein mat daalo.
  • Client state → jitna neeche ho sake utna neeche useState.
  • Derived → state banao hi mat, render mein calculate karo.
lessons.why: 90% "state management" ka dard asal mein server state ko client state ki tarah treat karne se aata hai. Server data ko caching, refetch, stale detection, dedup chahiye — Redux ye kuch nahi karta, isliye log ye sab haath se likhte hain. React Query ye sab free deta hai, aur phir bacha hua client state itna kam hota hai ki useState + Context kaafi ho jaata hai.

system design round ka common sawaal
pros: Server state alag karne se global store 80% chhota ho jaata hai
Derived state hatane se sync bugs khatam
Local state se component portable rehta hai
cons: Do alag systems (query + client store) seekhne padte hain
Sahi jagah decide karna judgement ka kaam hai
Galat decision baad mein refactor mehnga
gotchas: Server data ko Redux mein mat daalo — wo cache hai, state nahi
Jo props/state se calculate ho sakta hai wo state MAT banao
Filter, tab, page — ye URL mein rakho, useState mein nahi

lessons.name: Context API — Correct Usage
lessons.desc: Context is designed for low-frequency, global data (theme, auth, locale) — not high-frequency state updates that should use a dedicated store.
lessons.q: What is Context good for and what is it NOT good for? What performance problems does heavy Context use cause?
lessons.qsub: How would you implement a Context that doesn't re-render consumers when unrelated parts of the value change?
terms: jab koi Provider na ho tab milne wali value
useContext ko apne hook mein lapetna — safety ke liye
lessons.what: Definition: Context ka sahi tarika: hamesha ek custom hook banao jo Provider missing hone pe error de, value ko useMemo karo, aur data + actions ko alag context mein rakho.
lessons.why: Bina wrapper ke useContext(Ctx) Provider bhoolne pe null deta hai — aur crash 3 file door hota hai, samajh nahi aata kyun. Custom hook mein throw karo to error exactly wahin milta hai aur message clear hota hai.
pros: Custom hook se Provider missing ka error turant aur clear
Split context se bewajah re-render bach jaata hai
Type-safe — null check ke baad TS ko pata hai value hai
cons: Boilerplate badh jaata hai (2 context, 2 hooks)
Selector support nahi — partial subscribe nahi kar sakte
Nested providers se tree gehra ho jaata hai
gotchas: Provider value hamesha useMemo — sabse aam performance bug yahi hai
createContext ka default value sirf tab milta hai jab Provider ho hi na — usse "default state" mat samjho
Ek hi bade context mein sab kuch mat daalo — badalne wale hisse alag karo

lessons.name: Redux — Core Concepts & Middleware
lessons.desc: Single store, pure reducers, actions as intent. Middleware (thunk, saga) handles side effects. Selectors compute derived state. DevTools enable time-travel debugging.
lessons.q: Explain the full Redux data flow. What is the role of middleware? When is Redux overkill?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between Redux Thunk and Redux Saga? What problem does each solve?
terms: ek jagah jahan poore app ka state hai
plain object jo batata hai kya hua
action aur reducer ke beech ka layer — logging, async, etc.
lessons.what:
Definition: Redux ek predictable state container hai. Teen niyam: (1) single store, (2) state read-only — sirf action dispatch karke badlo, (3) badlav pure reducers se hote hain.

Data flow ek hi direction mein: dispatch(action) → middleware → reducer → naya state → UI.
lessons.analogy: Court ka record room. Koi file seedha nahi badal sakta. Application (action) do, clerk (reducer) rules dekh ke naya record banata hai, purana record bhi hamesha traceable rehta hai.
lessons.why:
Redux ka asli fayda traceability hai — DevTools mein har action, har state change, time-travel debugging. Bade team wale complex apps mein "ye state kisne badla" ka jawab 5 second mein mil jaata hai.

Par 2026 mein plain Redux mat likho — Redux Toolkit use karo. Aur server data ke liye Redux use hi mat karo, React Query lo.

pros: DevTools time-travel — debugging ka sabse strong tool
Predictable — same actions, same state
Middleware se cross-cutting logic (log, analytics, persist)
cons: Boilerplate bahut zyada (RTK se kam hota hai)
Server data ke liye galat tool
Chhote/medium app ke liye overkill
gotchas: Reducer mein state mutate mat karo — plain Redux mein Immer nahi hai
Reducer mein fetch/random/Date.now mat karo — pure honi chahiye
useSelector object return kare to har baar naya reference — shallowEqual ya alag selectors use karo

lessons.name: Redux Toolkit — Modern Redux
lessons.desc: RTK eliminates Redux boilerplate: createSlice merges actions+reducers, createAsyncThunk handles async flows, RTK Query handles server state.
lessons.q: What problems does Redux Toolkit solve over vanilla Redux? Explain createSlice and createAsyncThunk.
lessons.qsub: How does Immer work inside RTK to allow "mutable" reducer code while keeping immutability?
terms: reducer + actions ek saath banata hai
library jo "mutate" likhne deta hai par andar se immutable copy banata hai
RTK ka data fetching + caching layer
lessons.what: Definition: Redux Toolkit aaj Redux likhne ka official tarika hai. createSlice ek hi jagah state, reducers aur actions bana deta hai. Immer built-in hai isliye tum state.count++ likh sakte ho — dikhne mein mutation, andar se immutable.
lessons.why:
Plain Redux mein ek feature ke liye 4 files chahiye thi — actions, types, reducer, selectors. RTK mein ek slice file. Aur Immer ki wajah se nested update ka spread-hell khatam:

Purana: {...s, a:{...s.a, b:{...s.a.b, c:1}}} → RTK: s.a.b.c = 1
where: purane Redux se dheere dheere slice-by-slice
agar server data bhi Redux mein hi rakhna ho
pros: Boilerplate 70% kam
Immer se nested update bilkul aasan
TypeScript support bahut achha — actions ke types apne aap
cons: Bundle size Zustand se bada
Abhi bhi Redux ka mental model seekhna padta hai
Immer ka magic beginners ko confuse karta hai
gotchas: Immer sirf createSlice ke ANDAR chalta hai — bahar mutate karoge to bug
Reducer mein mutate karo YA naya state return karo — dono ek saath mat karo
createAsyncThunk mein pending/fulfilled/rejected teeno handle karo, warna loading atak jaayega

lessons.name: Zustand — Lightweight Store
lessons.desc: A minimal store based on closures and subscriptions. Components subscribe to slices — only re-render when their subscribed slice changes, unlike Context.
lessons.q: How does Zustand work under the hood? How does it avoid the re-render problem that Context has?
lessons.qsub: Compare Zustand, Context+useReducer, and Redux for a mid-size app. What are the tradeoffs?
terms: ek hook jo state deta hai — create() se banta hai
store ka sirf ek hissa chunna — sirf usi pe re-render
object ki top-level keys compare karna
lessons.what:
Definition: Zustand ek chhota (~1KB) state library hai. Store banate ho create() se, aur wo ek hook ban jaata hai. Koi Provider nahi, koi boilerplate nahi.

Sabse bada farak Context se: selector support. Tum store ka sirf ek field subscribe kar sakte ho — baaki kuch bhi badle, tumhara component render nahi hoga.
lessons.why: Context mein value badla to sab consumers render hote hain. Zustand mein useStore(s => s.count) likhne se sirf count badalne pe render hota hai. Isliye tez-badalne wale global state ke liye Zustand sahi hai aur Context galat.
where: store ko component ke bahar se bhi use kar sakte ho
pros: Bahut chhota aur seekhne mein 10 minute
Selector se precise re-render control
No Provider — testing aur setup aasan
cons: Redux DevTools jitna powerful time-travel nahi (middleware se milta hai)
Structure enforce nahi karta — bade team mein anarchy ho sakti hai
Server state ke liye phir bhi React Query chahiye
gotchas: Selector zaroor use karo — useCart() poora store leke aata hai aur har change pe render karega
Object return karne wale selector ke saath useShallow lagao, warna har baar naya reference
Store ke andar set() mein purana state spread karo warna baaki fields udd jaayenge

lessons.name: React Query / TanStack Query
lessons.desc: Manages server state: caching, background refetching, stale-while-revalidate, pagination, optimistic updates. Removes the need for loading/error/data state boilerplate.
lessons.q: What problem does React Query solve that useState+useEffect doesn't? Explain stale-while-revalidate.
lessons.qsub: How does React Query handle cache invalidation? What is the difference between queryKey and staleTime?
terms: cache ki unique pehchan — array hoti hai
data purana ho gaya — background mein refetch hoga
server pe data badalne wala operation (POST/PUT/DELETE)
lessons.what: Definition: TanStack Query server data ke liye ek cache hai, state manager nahi. Ye handle karta hai: caching, deduplication (2 component ne same data maanga = 1 request), background refetch, stale-while-revalidate, retry, pagination, optimistic updates.
lessons.analogy: Fridge. Doodh server pe hai, tumhare fridge mein uski copy hai. Purani ho jaaye to background mein naya mangwa lete ho — par tab tak purani hi use karte ho, khali nahi baithte.
lessons.why: useEffect + useState se data fetch karne mein ye sab tumhe khud likhna padta hai: loading/error state, race condition guard, cache, dedup, refetch on focus, retry, pagination. React Query mein ye sab 3 line mein aa jaata hai — isliye ye 2026 mein server data ka default answer hai.

gotchas: Query key mein har wo variable daalo jo queryFn use karta hai — warna stale data milega
staleTime 0 default hai — har mount pe refetch hota hai, use set karo
React Query se aaya data ko useState mein copy mat karo — wahi cache use karo

lessons.name: Atomic State — Recoil & Jotai
lessons.desc: Atom-based state: tiny, composable units of state. Components subscribe to only the atoms they need — minimal re-renders with a graph-based dependency model.
lessons.q: What is atomic state management? How do atoms differ from a single global store like Redux?
lessons.qsub: What is a selector in Recoil/Jotai? How does derived state work in atomic models?
terms: doosre atoms se banaya gaya atom
chhote tukdo se bada banana — top-down store ka ulta
lessons.what:
Definition: Atomic state (Jotai, Recoil) mein ek bada store nahi hota — bahut saare chhote atoms hote hain. Har component sirf jo atom use karta hai usi pe subscribe hota hai.

Derived atoms doosre atoms se apne aap calculate ho jaate hain — aur sirf tab recompute hote hain jab unka koi dependency badle.
lessons.analogy: Excel. Har cell ek atom hai. =A1+B1 derived cell hai. A1 badla to sirf wahi formula chala jo A1 pe depend karta hai — poori sheet dobara calculate nahi hoti.
lessons.why: Zustand/Redux mein tumhe selector likhna padta hai taaki extra render na ho. Atomic model mein subscription apne aap precise hai — tumne atom use kiya, bas usi pe subscribe ho gaye. Aur derived atom se "computed state" ka poora dependency graph React khud sambhalta hai.
where: jab Context ki re-render problem chubhne lage
pros: Subscription apne aap precise — selector likhne ki zaroorat nahi
Derived atoms ka dependency graph automatic
Async atoms Suspense ke saath natural
cons: Bahut saare atoms ho jaayein to organize karna mushkil
Recoil ab maintain nahi ho raha — Jotai lo
DevTools Redux jitne mature nahi
gotchas: Atoms ko component ke ANDAR mat banao — har render naya atom = state reset
useAtomValue (read-only) aur useSetAtom (write-only) use karo — useAtom dono karta hai aur bewajah render bhi
Recoil ke tutorials mile to Jotai dekho — Recoil practically dead hai

lessons.name: Understanding Re-renders
lessons.desc: A component re-renders when: its state changes, its parent re-renders, context it consumes changes, or its key changes. Props being the same is NOT enough to prevent re-renders.
lessons.q: List every cause of a React re-render. What is the most common source of unnecessary re-renders in production apps?
lessons.qsub: If a parent re-renders but passes the same props to a child, does the child re-render? What stops it?
terms: browser ka pixels dobara banana — ye alag cheez hai
React ka render skip kar dena
lessons.what:
Definition: Component sirf 4 wajah se re-render hota hai:

  1. Uska apna state badla
  2. Uska parent re-render hua
  3. Uska koi context value badla
  4. Uske hook (useSyncExternalStore etc.) ne update bheja

Props badalna list mein nahi hai — props tabhi badalte hain jab parent render hua, to asli wajah #2 hai.
lessons.why: Sabse bada misconception: "props badle isliye render hua". Sach ulta hai — parent render hua isliye child render hua, chahe props bilkul same hon. Ye samajhne se optimization ka sahi rasta dikhta hai: props memo karne se pehle parent ka render rokna ya state ko neeche push karna zyada asardar hai.

pros: Chaar wajah — poori list yahi hai, aur kuch nahi
State neeche push karna sabse saaf fix hai
Composition memo se behtar aur sasta hai
cons: Bade tree mein wajah dhoondhna time leta hai
Har render slow nahi hota — pehle naapo
gotchas: Re-render ka matlab DOM update NAHI hai — React diff karke aksar kuch nahi badalta
"Props same hain to render nahi hoga" — GALAT. memo ke bina hoga.
Pehle state ko neeche push karo, memo aakhri option hai

lessons.name: React.memo — Shallow Comparison
lessons.desc: Wraps a component to memoize its render. Skips re-render if props are shallowly equal. Fails silently with object/array/function props created inline.
lessons.q: How does React.memo work? Why does it often fail to prevent re-renders with object or function props?
lessons.qsub: Is React.memo free? What is its cost, and when does the overhead outweigh the benefit?
terms: HOC jo props same hone par re-render skip karta hai
har prop ko Object.is se compare — andar nahi jhaankta
lessons.what:
Definition: React.memo(Component) component ko lapet deta hai. Parent render hone par React pehle props ko shallow compare karta hai — sab same hain to component ko chalata hi nahi.

Shallow = har prop pe Object.is. Object ke andar nahi dekhta, sirf reference.
lessons.why: Isiliye memo aksar "kaam nahi karta" — parent inline object/array/function bhej raha hai jo har render naya reference hai. Memo dekhta hai reference alag, aur render kar deta hai. Fix: parent mein useMemo/useCallback, ya primitives pass karo.
where: hazaar rows mein sabse zyada fayda
jo aksar same props pate hain
pros: Bade subtree ka render bach jaata hai
List rows mein bahut fark padta hai
Custom comparator se fine control
cons: Compare ki apni cost — chhote component pe nuksaan
Inline props se aksar chup-chaap toot jaata hai
Custom comparator galat likho to stale UI
gotchas: children prop memo ko lagbhag hamesha tod deta hai — JSX har baar naya element object hai
Har component ko memo mat karo — compare ki cost render se zyada ho sakti hai
Comparator ka true matlab "SAME hai, skip karo" — shouldComponentUpdate ka ULTA

lessons.name: memo + useMemo + useCallback Triad
lessons.desc: React.memo + useCallback is the classic pattern: memo prevents re-render, useCallback prevents the function reference from changing on every parent render.
lessons.q: Explain the React.memo + useCallback pattern. When is it necessary and when is it premature optimization?
lessons.qsub: What is the "object identity" problem in React? Give 3 examples of places where it causes unexpected re-renders.
terms: teeno ka saath mein kaam karna
ek toota to poori chain bekaar
lessons.what:
Definition: Teeno alag cheezein hain par saath mein kaam karti hain:

  • React.memo — component ka render rokta hai
  • useMemo — value ka reference stable rakhta hai
  • useCallback — function ka reference stable rakhta hai

Rule: React.memo ke bina baaki dono bekaar hain (except effect deps ke liye).
lessons.analogy: Taala aur chaabi. React.memo taala hai. useMemo/useCallback chaabi ko same rakhte hain. Taala na ho to chaabi ka koi matlab nahi — darwaza waise hi khula hai.
lessons.why: Chain mein ek bhi kadi tooti to poora effort bekaar. Isliye memoize karne ka sahi tarika hai: pehle Profiler se naapo, phir poori chain banao, phir dobara naapo ki sach mein fark pada. Andaaze se lagaya hua memo aksar sirf cost hai.

List performance mein saaf fark
Effect loops rukte hain
cons: Code padhne mein bhaari ho jaata hai
Chain ek jagah tooti to poora effort waste
Har jagah lagana aksar net negative hota hai
gotchas: Pehle naapo, phir memo karo, phir dobara naapo — bina naape memo aksar nuksaan hai
Composition (children as props) memo se sasta aur saaf hai — pehle wo try karo
React 19 compiler ye automatic karta hai — check karo project mein enabled hai ya nahi

lessons.name: Code Splitting — React.lazy + Suspense
lessons.desc: React.lazy() enables dynamic import() for components. Suspense shows a fallback while the bundle loads. Reduces initial bundle size and TTI.
lessons.q: How does React.lazy and Suspense work? What is the network request pattern it generates?
lessons.qsub: How would you implement route-based code splitting in a React app? What about component-level splitting?
terms: saara JS ek file mein — bada ho to page late khulta hai
bundle ka alag tukda jo alag se download hota hai
zaroorat padne pe hi load karna
lessons.what:
Definition: Code splitting bade bundle ko chhote chunks mein todna hai, jo tabhi download hote hain jab chahiye. React mein React.lazy() + <Suspense> se.

lazy(() => import('./X')) ek dynamic import hai — bundler ise dekhkar X ko alag file bana deta hai.
lessons.analogy: Netflix. Poori movie library download nahi karte — jo dekhna hai bas wahi stream hota hai.
lessons.why: Har KB JS ko download + parse + execute karna padta hai. Mobile pe 1MB bundle 3-4 second kha jaata hai. Agar admin panel, chart library, aur rich text editor sirf 5% users ko chahiye, to unhe sabke initial load mein daalna galat hai.
where: jab tak khule nahi tab tak load nahi
pros: Initial bundle chhota — first paint tez
User jo use nahi karta wo download hi nahi hota
Preload se perceived speed aur behtar
cons: Bahut zyada split karo to network waterfall ban jaata hai
Fallback UI galat size ka ho to layout shift
Chunk load fail ho sakta hai — error boundary chahiye
gotchas: lazy() component ko component ke ANDAR define mat karo — har render naya import
Fallback ki height asli content jaisi rakho warna page kood jaayega (CLS)
Chunk load failure handle karo — deploy ke baad purane chunk 404 dete hain

lessons.name: List Virtualization
lessons.desc: Only render DOM nodes for visible items. Libraries like react-window and TanStack Virtual keep a constant-size DOM regardless of list length.
lessons.q: What is list virtualization? Explain how react-window implements it. What are its limitations?
lessons.qsub: When is virtualization NOT the right solution? What are the accessibility and scroll-to-index challenges?
terms: sirf jo dikh raha hai utne hi DOM nodes banana
screen ka wo hissa jo abhi dikhta hai
window ke thoda upar-neeche extra rows — scroll smooth rahe
lessons.what: Definition: 10,000 rows ka DOM banana browser ko maar dalta hai. Virtualization mein sirf ~20 visible rows ka DOM banta hai; scroll pe unhi nodes ko naye data ke saath reuse kar liya jaata hai. Poori list ki height ek spacer div se fake ki jaati hai taaki scrollbar sahi lage.
lessons.analogy: Train ki khidki. Poora raasta ek saath nahi dikhta — bas utna jitna khidki se dikhe. Train aage badhti hai, khidki mein naya drishya aa jaata hai.
lessons.why: Har DOM node ki memory + layout cost hai. 10,000 rows = 10,000+ nodes = browser 5-10 second freeze. Virtualized list mein 20 nodes rehte hain, isliye 10,000 aur 1,000,000 rows lagbhag same speed pe chalte hain.

cons: Ctrl+F se page search kaam nahi karta (DOM mein hai hi nahi)

Row ki estimated height galat ho to scrollbar kood-ta hai

lessons.name: React Profiler & DevTools
lessons.desc: The Profiler API and DevTools flamegraph show render durations, commit counts, and which component triggered a render — the starting point for any perf investigation.
lessons.q: How do you identify performance bottlenecks in a React app? Walk me through your debugging process.
lessons.qsub: What does the "why did this render?" feature in React DevTools tell you? What is the Profiler API for?
terms: React DevTools ka tab jo render measure karta hai
chart jisme har component ka render time bar ki tarah dikhta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: React DevTools Profiler record karta hai ki kaunsa component kab, kitni der, aur kyun render hua. Ye "why did this render" ka jawab andaaze se nahi, data se deta hai.

<Profiler> component se tum programmatically bhi timings collect kar sakte ho.
lessons.why: Optimization ka pehla rule — naapo, andaaza mat lagao. Log aksar galat jagah memo lagate hain aur asli problem (ek bhaari sort, ya context ka poora tree render) chhoot jaati hai. Profiler 2 minute mein sach dikha deta hai.
where: memo lagaane ke baad dobara naapo
Profiler API se render time regression test
pros: Asli data — andaaza khatam
"Why did this render" seedha wajah batata hai
Ranked view se culprit turant milta hai
cons: Profiling khud thoda overhead daalta hai
Production build mein DevTools kam detail deta hai
Flamegraph padhna seekhna padta hai
gotchas: "Record why each component rendered" setting on karo — ye default OFF hai aur yahi sabse kaam ki cheez hai
Dev build production se dheema hota hai — absolute numbers nahi, RELATIVE dekho
StrictMode dev mein double render karta hai — profiling mein isse account karo

lessons.name: Composition as a Performance Tool
lessons.desc: Lifting static children via props.children or slot props means they are created by the parent, not the child — so they don't re-render when the child's state changes.
lessons.q: How can component composition prevent unnecessary re-renders without using React.memo?
lessons.qsub: Explain the "children as props" performance optimization with a concrete example (e.g. a context consumer that wraps expensive children).
terms: component ko props/children ke through jodna
JSX ko prop ki tarah pass karna
React element ka wahi object hona
lessons.what: Definition: Agar tum JSX ko parent ke bahar banate ho aur children prop se andar bhejte ho, to us element ka reference badalta nahi. Jab wrapper ka state badalta hai, React children ko same element dekh kar uska render skip kar deta hai — bina memo lagaaye.
lessons.analogy: Tiffin. Khana ghar pe bana (bahar) aur dabbe mein rakh diya. Dabba (wrapper) rang badalta rahe, khana dobara nahi banega.
lessons.why: Ye memo se behtar hai kyunki: koi comparison cost nahi, koi useCallback/useMemo chain nahi, aur code padhne mein normal lagta hai. Isliye rule ye hai — pehle composition try karo, memo aakhri raasta.

cons: Har case mein possible nahi — child ko parent ka state chahiye ho to nahi chalega
Component structure ko refactor karna padta hai
gotchas: Ye tabhi kaam karta hai jab children ko parent ka state NAHI chahiye
Provider ke andar children ko as-props hi rakho, andar JSX mat likho
Optimization ke liye pehle YE try karo, React.memo baad mein

lessons.name: Concurrent Mode & Interruptible Rendering
lessons.desc: React can now pause, interrupt, and restart rendering work. High-priority updates (user input) can interrupt low-priority renders in progress.
lessons.q: What is Concurrent Mode? How does interruptible rendering improve user experience?
lessons.qsub: What is "tearing" in concurrent React? How do useSyncExternalStore and concurrent-mode-safe state managers prevent it?
terms: ek se zyada UI version ek saath tayyar rakhna
render beech mein rok ke baad mein resume karna
kaunsa update turant chahiye, kaunsa ruk sakta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Concurrent React ka matlab hai ki React ek render ko rok, resume, ya phenk sakta hai. Ye koi feature nahi jise "on" karte ho — ye ek capability hai jo createRoot se milti hai, aur jise tum useTransition/useDeferredValue/Suspense se use karte ho.

Parallel nahi hai — JS abhi bhi single-threaded hai. Ye sirf smart scheduling hai.
lessons.analogy: Ek hi cook, do orders. Wo dono ek saath nahi banata — par urgent order aaye to dhima wala kaam beech mein rok deta hai, urgent nipta ke wapas aata hai.
lessons.why: Purane React mein ek render shuru hua to poora hoke hi rukta tha. Bhaari list render karte waqt tumhara typing freeze ho jaata tha. Concurrent mein React kehta hai "typing zyada zaroori hai" — list ka aadha render phenk deta hai, typing dikhata hai, phir list dobara shuru karta hai.
