lessons.name: Suspense — Data Fetching & Code Splitting
lessons.desc: Suspense catches "not ready yet" signals from lazy components or data libraries, shows a fallback, and re-renders when data is ready — enabling a waterfall-free fetch-on-render model.
lessons.q: How does Suspense work for data fetching vs code splitting? What does a library need to do to support Suspense?
lessons.qsub: What is the "fetch-then-render" vs "render-as-you-fetch" pattern? How does Suspense enable the latter?
terms: boundary jo "abhi ready nahi" wale children ke liye fallback dikhata hai
jab tak ready na ho tab tak dikhne wala UI
component ka "main abhi tayyar nahi" bolna (promise throw karke)
lessons.what:
Definition: <Suspense fallback={...}> ek boundary hai. Uske andar ka koi component agar "abhi ready nahi" ho (lazy chunk load ho raha ho, ya data aa raha ho), to React fallback dikhata hai aur ready hote hi asli content.

Isse loading state component ke andar se nikal kar tree ke structure mein aa jaati hai.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant mein khaali plate rakhna. Khana aane tak plate (fallback) rehti hai — table khaali nahi dikhti. Khana aate hi plate hat jaati hai.
lessons.why:
Bina Suspense ke har component mein if (loading) return <Spinner/> likhna padta tha — 10 components = 10 alag spinner, page phatak-phatak karta tha. Suspense mein tum ek jagah decide karte ho ki poore section ka loading UI kya hoga.

Zaroori: plain useEffect fetch Suspense trigger nahi karta. Suspense ke liye Suspense-enabled source chahiye — React Query (suspense mode), RSC, framework loader, ya use().
where: server se HTML tukdon mein bhejna
pros: Loading state declarative — tree se dikhti hai
Nested boundaries se granular control
Waterfall kam hota hai (parallel fetch)
cons: Suspense-enabled data source chahiye
Error ke liye alag ErrorBoundary
Galat jagah boundary lagane se poora page waiting mein chala jaata hai
gotchas: useEffect wala fetch Suspense trigger NAHI karta — bahut log yahin atakte hain
Boundary jitni upar hogi utna bada hissa fallback mein jaayega — chhoti boundaries lagao
Suspense error handle nahi karta — ErrorBoundary alag se chahiye

lessons.name: useTransition & startTransition
lessons.desc: Mark a state update as non-urgent. React can interrupt and defer it in favour of urgent updates like typing. Returns [isPending, startTransition].
lessons.q: What does useTransition do? Give a concrete example where it prevents the UI from feeling sluggish.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between useTransition and debouncing? When would you use each?
terms: wo update jo ruk sakta hai — non-urgent
boolean jo batata hai transition chal raha hai
lessons.what:
Definition: const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition(). startTransition(fn) ke andar ke state updates ko React non-urgent maanta hai — koi urgent update aaya to inhe rok deta hai ya discard karke dobara chalata hai.

isPending se tum "loading" feel de sakte ho bina purana content hataye.
lessons.analogy: Waiter jo tumhara bada order le raha hai. Beech mein koi paani maange to wo pehle paani deta hai, phir order pe wapas aata hai.
lessons.why: Search box ka classic problem: har keystroke pe 5000 items filter hote hain. Bina transition ke typing lag karti hai. Transition ke saath: input ka state sync (turant dikhta hai) aur list ka state transition (ruk sakta hai). User ko typing hamesha instant lagti hai.
where: bhaari tab ke content ko transition mein
naya page load hote waqt purana dikhaate raho
pros: Input hamesha responsive rehta hai
isPending se saaf loading feedback
Purana content dikhta rehta hai — blank screen nahi
cons: Sab kuch transition mein daalna cheezon ko aur dheema kar deta hai
Async ke saath sambhal ke use karna padta hai
Sirf concurrent root mein kaam karta hai
gotchas: Controlled input ka setState kabhi transition mein mat daalo — typing lag karegi
await ke baad ke updates transition ke bahar hote hain
Sirf tab use karo jab render sach mein bhaari ho — warna faayda nahi

lessons.name: useDeferredValue
lessons.desc: Returns a deferred version of a value — React shows the stale value while re-rendering with the new value in the background.
lessons.q: What is the difference between useDeferredValue and useTransition? When would you reach for one over the other?
lessons.qsub: How does useDeferredValue combine with React.memo to create a "tearing"-free slow list filter?
terms: fixed time wait karna — timing tumhare haath mein
lessons.what:
Definition: const deferred = useDeferredValue(value) value ka ek "peechhe chalne wala" version deta hai. React pehle nayi value ke saath urgent UI update karta hai, phir background mein deferred value ke saath dobara render karta hai.

Farak useTransition se: transition mein tum update ko wrap karte ho (source pe control chahiye); deferred value mein tum value ko wrap karte ho — source kisi aur ka ho tab bhi chalta hai (props, library ka hook).
lessons.why: Debounce fixed 300ms wait karta hai chahe device tez ho ya dheema. useDeferredValue adaptive hai — tez device pe lagbhag turant, dheeme device pe zyada wait. Aur ye interruptible hai, isliye typing kabhi block nahi hoti.

pros: Device ke hisaab se adapt karta hai
Source pe control na ho tab bhi chalta hai
Interruptible — typing block nahi hoti
cons: Child memo nahi hai to koi fayda nahi
isPending nahi milta — khud compare karna padta hai
Network wait ke liye ye nahi hai (uske liye debounce)
gotchas: Deferred value use karne wala child React.memo mein hona CHAHIYE, warna bekaar
Network request kam karne ke liye ye nahi hai — wahan debounce chahiye
stale = (value !== deferred) se apna pending indicator banao

lessons.name: React Server Components (RSC)
lessons.desc: Components that run only on the server — zero JS in the bundle, direct database/filesystem access, no hooks or state. Client Components still run on both.
lessons.q: What are React Server Components? What can and can't they do? How do they differ from SSR?
lessons.qsub: What is the RSC "boundary"? How do you pass data from a Server Component to a Client Component?
terms: React Server Component — server pe chalta hai, browser mein kabhi nahi
purana normal component — browser mein chalta hai
file ke top pe likha directive jo boundary banata hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Server Components sirf server pe render hote hain. Unka JavaScript browser ko bheja hi nahi jaata — sirf render ka natija (ek special serialized format) jaata hai.

Isliye unme state, effects, event handlers nahi ho sakte. Par wo async ho sakte hain aur seedha DB query kar sakte hain.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant ki kitchen. Khana kitchen mein banta hai (server), tumhe sirf plate milti hai. Recipe, masale, chulha — kuch bhi tumhare table pe nahi aata.
lessons.why: Do bade fayde: (1) bundle size — markdown parser, date library, ORM ka code browser mein jaata hi nahi; (2) data access — component seedha DB se padh sakta hai, koi API layer nahi chahiye, koi client-server waterfall nahi.

DB seedha access — API layer ki zaroorat nahi
Secrets safely use kar sakte ho

Debugging mushkil — error server pe hoti hai

Server component ko client component ke andar IMPORT mat karo — children se pass karo
Server se client ko sirf serializable props ja sakte hain — function pass nahi kar sakte

lessons.name: Streaming SSR & Selective Hydration
lessons.desc: React 18's renderToPipeableStream streams HTML as it's ready. Selective hydration lets React prioritise hydrating the part the user interacts with first.
lessons.q: How does streaming SSR work? What is selective hydration and why does it improve interactivity (TTI)?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between renderToString (React 17) and renderToPipeableStream (React 18)?
terms: server ke HTML pe client JS ko "jodna" taaki interactive ho
HTML tukdon mein bhejna, poora ban-ne ka intezaar kiye bina
lessons.what:
Definition: Purana SSR "all-or-nothing" tha — poora page ka data aane tak kuch nahi bheja jaata tha. Streaming SSR mein server jo ready hai wo turant bhej deta hai, aur baaki tukde baad mein aate hain, Suspense boundaries ke hisaab se.

Selective hydration — React un hisson ko pehle interactive banata hai jinse user interact kar raha hai.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant mein starter pehle. Poore khane ka intezaar nahi karte — jo ready hai wo aata rehta hai.
lessons.why: Purane SSR mein ek slow API poore page ko rok deti thi — TTFB 3 second. Streaming mein header/nav turant dikh jaate hain, feed 2 second baad slot mein bhar jaata hai. Aur selective hydration se jis button pe user ne click kiya wo pehle interactive hota hai, chahe upar wala section abhi hydrate ho raha ho.

pros: TTFB aur FCP bahut behtar
Slow data poore page ko nahi rokta
Selective hydration se interactivity jaldi
cons: Hydration mismatch ke bugs
Streaming ke saath error handling complex
CDN/proxy setup dhyan se chahiye
gotchas: Suspense boundary ke bina streaming ka koi fayda nahi — boundaries lagao
Fallback ka size asli content jaisa rakho, warna layout shift
Server aur client ka pehla render EXACTLY same hona chahiye — Date.now/random mismatch degi

lessons.name: use() Hook & Async Components
lessons.desc: The use() hook (React 19+) reads resources like Promises or Context inside render — unwrapping Promises and suspending automatically.
lessons.q: What does the use() hook do? How does it differ from await and useEffect for async data?
lessons.qsub: What are the rules for use() that make it different from other hooks (can be called conditionally)?
terms: naya React API jo promise ya context "padh" leta hai
promise se andar ki value nikalna
if ke andar call karna — use() ke liye ye allowed hai
lessons.what:
Definition: use(promise) promise ko unwrap karta hai — jab tak resolve na ho, component suspend ho jaata hai (Suspense fallback dikhta hai). use(context) context bhi padh sakta hai.

Ye "hook" hai par baaki hooks jaisa nahi — ye conditionally aur loops mein call ho sakta hai.
lessons.why: Server component async ho sakta hai, par client component nahi. use() client component ko bhi promise ka intezaar karne deta hai. Isse pattern banta hai: server promise banata hai (await nahi karta) aur client ko pass karta hai — server render block nahi hota, aur client Suspense ke saath wait kar leta hai.
pros: Conditional call allowed — baaki hooks se alag
Server aur client ka data flow clean
Suspense ke saath natural
cons: Promise stable rakhna consumer ki zimmedari hai
React 19+ aur framework support chahiye
Debugging mushkil jab promise galti se recreate ho jaaye
gotchas: Render ke andar naya promise mat banao — cache ya props se aana chahiye, warna infinite loop
use() sirf render ke dauraan chalta hai — event handler ya effect mein nahi
Error ke liye ErrorBoundary chahiye, warna crash

lessons.name: Higher-Order Components (HOC)
lessons.desc: A function that takes a component and returns an enhanced component — the classic pre-hooks reuse pattern. Now largely replaced by custom hooks.
lessons.q: What is an HOC? What problems does it solve and what problems does it create (wrapper hell, prop collision)?
lessons.qsub: Why did custom hooks largely replace HOCs? In what scenarios do HOCs still make sense?
terms: function jo component leta hai aur naya component return karta hai
kai HOC nest hone se DevTools mein 8 layer
wrapped component ke static properties copy karna
lessons.what:
Definition: Higher-Order Component ek function hai: Component → Component. Ye purana component leta hai aur usko kuch extra props/behaviour ke saath lapet ke naya component deta hai.

Aaj custom hooks ne iski jagah le li hai — par HOC abhi bhi kuch cases mein sahi hai (aur legacy code mein bahut milta hai).
lessons.analogy: Jacket. Aadmi wahi hai, par jacket pehen ke thand se bach jaata hai. Do jacket, teen jacket — har ek kuch add karti hai, par chalna mushkil ho jaata hai.
lessons.why:
Hooks se pehle logic reuse ka yahi tarika tha. Problem: 4 HOC lagane se DevTools mein withAuth(withTheme(withRouter(withData(X)))) dikhta tha, props kahan se aa rahe hain pata nahi chalta tha, aur TypeScript types nightmare ban jaate the.

Aaj HOC kab sahi hai: jab tumhe component ko lapetna hi ho — error boundary add karna, Suspense wrap karna, conditionally render rokna. Hook ye nahi kar sakta.
pros: Component ko wrap kar sakta hai — hook nahi kar sakta
Class components mein bhi chalta hai
Conditional rendering control
cons: Wrapper hell — DevTools bhar jaata hai
Prop collision — kaunsa prop kahan se aaya, pata nahi
TypeScript types likhna painful
gotchas: displayName zaroor set karo warna DevTools mein "Unknown" dikhega
hoist-non-react-statics use karo warna static properties gum ho jaayenge
HOC ko component ke ANDAR apply mat karo — har render naya type = remount

lessons.name: Render Props
lessons.desc: Sharing behaviour by passing a function as a prop that returns JSX. Gives the consumer full control over the rendered output.
lessons.q: What is the render props pattern? Compare it to HOCs and custom hooks for sharing logic.
lessons.qsub: What is the performance problem with render props inside render? How do you fix it?
terms: wo prop jiski value ek function hai jo JSX return karti hai
children ko function ki tarah pass karna
kya render hoga ye consumer decide kare
lessons.what:
Definition: Component logic rakhta hai aur rendering ka faisla consumer pe chhod deta hai — ek function prop ke through jise wo apna state deta hai.

<Mouse render={pos => <p>{pos.x}</p>} /> ya children-as-function.
lessons.why:
HOC se behtar tha kyunki props ka source saaf dikhta tha (function ka argument), aur dynamic composition possible thi. Par nesting ka apna problem tha — 3 render props = 3 level indentation.

Aaj bhi zinda hai jahan component ko DOM/layout ka control chahiye: virtualized lists, drag-drop, chart libraries, <AutoSizer>. Hook wahan kaam nahi karta kyunki DOM structure component ke haath mein hona chahiye.
pros: Props ka source bilkul saaf — function ka argument
Component DOM structure control kar sakta hai
Class components ke saath bhi chalta hai
cons: Nesting se code gehra ho jaata hai
Inline function har render naya — memo tootta hai
Zyadatar cases mein hook simpler hai
gotchas: Zyadatar cases mein custom hook use karo — render prop tabhi jab DOM control chahiye
Inline arrow function har render naya hai — memoized child ke saath dhyan do
Callback ke andar hooks call mat karo — wo React component nahi hai

lessons.name: Compound Components
lessons.desc: A parent component implicitly shares state with a set of child components via Context — creating expressive, flexible APIs like <Select> + <Select.Option>.
lessons.q: What is the compound component pattern? Build a Tabs component using it.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between implicit state sharing (Context) and explicit prop passing in compound components?
terms: kai components jo milkar ek unit banate hain
parent ka state jo children ko context se milta hai
user decide kare kaunsa hissa kahan ho
lessons.what: Definition: Ek parent component apne bacchon ko context se state deta hai. User <Tabs><Tabs.List><Tabs.Tab/></Tabs.List><Tabs.Panel/></Tabs> likhta hai — HTML ke <select>/<option> jaisa.
lessons.analogy: Chess set. Board, mohre, timer — alag alag cheezein, par saath mein ek game. Har piece ko game ke rules pata hain bina baar baar bataye.
lessons.why:
Alternative hai "props ka pahaad": <Tabs items={[...]} renderTab={} renderPanel={} tabClass="" panelClass="" /> — jaise-jaise zaroorat badhti hai props badhte jaate hain aur component gaddar ho jaata hai.

Compound mein layout ka control user ke paas hai — wo tabs ko neeche rakh sakta hai, beech mein kuch daal sakta hai, apna wrapper laga sakta hai. Sab shadcn/ui, Radix, Headless UI isi pattern pe hain.
where: jahan user ko structure control chahiye
pros: Props ka explosion khatam
Layout ka poora control user ke paas
HTML jaisa natural API
cons: Implicit context — dependency dikhti nahi
Galat jagah use karne pe runtime error
Zyada boilerplate chhote widgets ke liye
gotchas: Custom hook mein null check karke saaf error throw karo — "cannot read of null" se bachao
Context value hamesha useMemo karo
React.Children.map se children inspect karna avoid karo — nesting mein toot jaata hai

lessons.name: Error Boundaries
lessons.desc: Class components implementing getDerivedStateFromError / componentDidCatch that catch render errors in their subtree and show fallback UI.
lessons.q: What are Error Boundaries? What errors do they NOT catch? Why must they be class components?
lessons.qsub: Where would you place error boundaries in a production app? What should you log in componentDidCatch?
terms: class component jo apne bacchon ki render errors pakadta hai
error pe fallback UI dikhane ke liye state set karta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Error Boundary ek class component hai jo apne children ke render, lifecycle aur constructor ki errors pakadta hai aur crash ki jagah fallback UI dikhata hai.

Ye nahi pakadta: event handlers, async code (setTimeout, promise), server-side rendering, aur khud boundary ke andar ki error.
lessons.why: React 16 se ek uncaught error poore app ko unmount kar deta hai — user ko safed screen. Wajah: adha-toota UI dikhane se galat data dikh sakta hai (soch — payment page pe galat amount). Isliye React kehta hai "ya poora sahi, ya kuch nahi" — aur boundary se tum decide karo ki "kuch nahi" ki jagah kya dikhe.

Event handler / setTimeout / promise ki errors NAHI pakadta — wahan try/catch karo

lessons.name: Portals
lessons.desc: ReactDOM.createPortal renders children into a different DOM node than the parent — useful for modals and tooltips that need to escape overflow:hidden or z-index stacking.
lessons.q: What are Portals? Why do modals use them? How does event bubbling work through a Portal?
lessons.qsub: Even though a Portal renders outside its parent DOM node, does it still bubble React synthetic events through the React tree? Why?
terms: child ko DOM mein kahin aur render karna, tree mein wahin rakhte hue
CSS ka wo scope jisme z-index ki tulna hoti hai
event ka parent tak upar jaana
lessons.what: Definition: createPortal(children, domNode) children ko kisi bhi DOM node mein render karta hai — par React tree mein wo wahin rehta hai. Matlab context milta hai, events React parent tak bubble hote hain, par DOM mein wo document.body mein hai.
lessons.analogy: Video call. Tum ghar pe ho (React tree), par screen pe office meeting mein dikh rahe ho (DOM). Ghar wale se baat bhi kar sakte ho.
lessons.why:
Modal ka classic problem: parent pe overflow: hidden, transform, ya kam z-index ho to modal kat jaata hai ya peechhe chala jaata hai. Chahe tum z-index: 9999 lagao — transform naya stacking context banata hai, tumhara z-index us context ke andar hi kaam karta hai.

Portal se modal body ka direct child ban jaata hai — koi parent CSS use kaat nahi sakta.
pros: Parent ka overflow/z-index/transform affect nahi karta
Context aur React events normal chalte hain
Accessibility manage karna aasan
cons: Event React tree se bubble hote hain — confusing ho sakta hai
Focus trap khud likhna padta hai
SSR mein document nahi hota
gotchas: Event DOM tree se nahi, REACT tree se bubble hote hain — outside-click logic ismein galat ho jaata hai
SSR mein document.body nahi hai — mounted check lagao ya dialog element use karo
Focus trap, aria-modal, ESC, background scroll lock — sab khud karna padta hai (ya Radix Dialog use karo)

lessons.name: forwardRef & useImperativeHandle
lessons.desc: forwardRef passes a ref through a component to a child DOM node. useImperativeHandle customizes what the parent sees when it uses that ref.
lessons.q: When and why do you need forwardRef? What is the difference between forwardRef and useImperativeHandle?
lessons.qsub: Build an input component that exposes a .focus() method via ref to its parent without exposing the full DOM node.
terms: ref ko andar ke DOM node tak pahunchana
ref se kya kya milega wo customize karna
method call karke kaam karana (declarative ka ulta)
lessons.what:
Definition: ref normal prop nahi hai — React use alag treat karta hai, isliye wo apne aap child ke andar nahi jaata. forwardRef se tum use andar ke DOM node tak pahuncha sakte ho.

useImperativeHandle se tum ref ke through poora DOM node dene ki jagah sirf chuni hui methods de sakte ho.

React 19 mein ref ab normal prop hai — forwardRef ki zaroorat khatam.
lessons.why: Kabhi kabhi parent ko child ke DOM pe kaam karna hota hai — focus, scroll, video play/pause, form reset. Ye declarative props se nahi hota. Par poora DOM node de dena bhi galat hai (parent kuch bhi kar sakta hai) — useImperativeHandle se tum ek chhota controlled API dete ho.
where: React Hook Form input register karta hai
pros: Parent ko zaroori imperative control milta hai
useImperativeHandle se surface chhota rehta hai
React 19 mein syntax bahut simple ho gaya
cons: Imperative code declarative model ke khilaf hai
Types likhna thoda mushkil
Overuse se component ka contract gandaa ho jaata hai
gotchas: React 19 mein forwardRef deprecated hai — ref ab normal prop hai
useImperativeHandle ka deps array zaroor do warna har render naya object
Pehle sochо kya props se kaam ho sakta hai — imperative aakhri raasta hai

lessons.name: Provider Pattern & Dependency Injection
lessons.desc: Wrapping a subtree with a Provider to inject dependencies (services, config, state) without prop drilling — the foundation of most React library APIs.
lessons.q: How does the Provider pattern work in React? How is it used as dependency injection for testing?
lessons.qsub: How would you use the Provider pattern to make a component tree testable by swapping out real APIs with mocks?
terms: dependency bahar se dena, andar banane ki jagah
wo component jo dependency deta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Provider pattern mein tum services/config ko Context ke through tree mein daalte ho. Component sochta nahi ki API client kahan se aaya — bas useApi() maangta hai.

Ye React ka dependency injection hai.
lessons.why:
Agar component ke andar import { api } from './api' hai to test mein use replace karna mushkil hai — module mock karna padta hai. Provider se test mein bas nakli provider laga do, component ko pata bhi nahi chalega.

Aur multi-tenant/env-specific config (staging vs prod API) bhi isi se saaf handle hoti hai.
pros: Test mein dependency swap karna trivial
Component apni dependency khud nahi banata — reusable
Config ek jagah
cons: Provider hell — 8 nested providers
Dependency implicit hai, import se dikhti nahi
Context ki re-render problem yahan bhi hai
gotchas: Provider value ko useMemo karo, warna poora app har render pe re-render
Sab kuch ek Services context mein mat daalo — alag concerns alag context
compose helper se provider nesting flat rakho

lessons.name: Container / Presentational Split
lessons.desc: Separate data-fetching/logic (container) from pure rendering (presentational). Now done naturally with custom hooks extracting logic from display components.
lessons.q: What is the container/presentational pattern? How has it evolved with hooks?
lessons.qsub: Is this pattern still relevant with custom hooks? Describe a case where explicit containers still add value.
lessons.what:
Definition: Purana pattern — Container data laata hai aur logic rakhta hai, Presentational sirf props leke UI banata hai.

Aaj: hooks ne containers ki zaroorat lagbhag khatam kar di. Par idea zinda hai — bas ab wo "logic hook mein, UI component mein" ban gaya hai. RSC mein ye wapas strong ho gaya (server = container, client = presentational).
lessons.why:
Fayda ab bhi wahi hai: UI component ka test aasan hai (bas props do), Storybook mein dikhana aasan hai, aur reuse karna aasan hai (same UI alag data source ke saath).

Par har component ko do mein todna over-engineering hai. Todo tab jab UI reuse ho raha ho ya test/story likhni ho.
where: stories ke liye pure components chahiye
pros: UI component test karna trivial
Storybook mein har state dikhana aasan
Same UI alag data source ke saath reuse
cons: Har jagah lagane se bewajah files double
Props drilling badh sakti hai
Hooks ke baad container component aksar redundant hai
gotchas: Blindly har component ko mat todo — sirf jab reuse/test/story ka fayda ho
Aaj container ek HOOK hona chahiye, ek component nahi
Presentational component ko sach mein pure rakho — usme koi fetch/router/context nahi

lessons.name: React Testing Library Philosophy
lessons.desc: "Test the behaviour users see, not implementation details." Queries mirror what users and assistive technology perceive — avoiding brittle tests tied to component internals.
lessons.q: What is the React Testing Library philosophy? Why is testing implementation details harmful?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between getBy, queryBy, and findBy? When do you use each?
terms: React Testing Library — user ki tarah test karne wali library
element dhoondhne ka tarika — getByRole, getByText...
andar ka code jo user ko dikhta hi nahi
lessons.what:
Definition: RTL ka ek hi principle hai — "tests jitne zyada user ke istemaal jaise hon, utna zyada bharosa dete hain". Isliye RTL state, props, ya internal functions ko touch hi nahi karta. Wo sirf screen pe jo dikhta hai usse baat karta hai.

Query priority: getByRole > getByLabelText > getByText > ... > getByTestId (aakhri raasta).
lessons.analogy: Gaadi ka test drive. Tum engine kholke piston nahi ginte — chalake dekhte ho ki chalti hai, mudti hai, rukti hai. Engine badal do par chale to test pass hona chahiye.
lessons.why:
Implementation test karoge to har refactor pe test tootenge — chahe app bilkul theek chal raha ho. Wo test tumhe rokta hai, bachata nahi. RTL wale test refactor mein zinda rehte hain aur sach mein tootne par hi fail hote hain.

Bonus: getByRole use karne se accessibility apne aap test ho jaati hai — agar button ka accessible name nahi hai to query fail hogi.

jsdom asli browser nahi — layout, scroll sab fake

lessons.name: What to Test in React
lessons.desc: Test: user interactions, rendered output, async state changes, error states. Do NOT test: internal state, component method calls, or prop types.
lessons.q: What makes a good React component test? What should you avoid testing and why?
lessons.qsub: How do you test a component that fetches data? Walk through setup, render, assert pattern.
terms: Kent C. Dodds ka model — integration tests sabse zyada
kitna code test se chhua gaya — quality ka proof nahi
purana feature naye change se toot jaana
lessons.what:
Definition: Sab kuch test karna waste hai. Test wahi karo jahan toot-ne ka nuksaan zyada ho:

  1. User flows — login, checkout, form submit
  2. Business logic — price calculation, permission, validation
  3. Edge cases — empty, error, loading, bahut lamba text
  4. Purane bugs — har fix ke saath ek test (regression)
lessons.why:
Traditional pyramid (bahut saare unit tests) React mein galat fit hai kyunki React ke bugs aksar components ke beech hote hain, andar nahi. Isliye "trophy" model — integration tests sabse zyada value dete hain: ek test jo form bhare, submit kare, aur result check kare, 10 unit tests se zyada bharosa deta hai.

100% coverage ka peechha mat karo — wo sirf batata hai code chala, ye nahi ki sahi chala.

har fix ke saath ek regression test

Refactor confidently kar sakte ho
Test dastavez ki tarah kaam karte hain
cons: Integration tests dheere hote hain
Setup zyada lagta hai
Kya test karna hai ye judgement ka kaam hai
gotchas: 100% coverage ka target mat rakho — wo quality nahi naapta
Har bug fix ke saath ek test likho — wahi sabse valuable test hota hai
Third-party library ko test mat karo — wo unka kaam hai

lessons.name: Mocking — MSW & jest.mock
lessons.desc: MSW (Mock Service Worker) intercepts at network level — most realistic. jest.mock replaces modules. Both have their place; MSW is preferred for API tests.
lessons.q: What is MSW and why is it better than mocking fetch/axios directly in tests?
lessons.qsub: How do you mock a custom hook in tests? Is that a good idea?
terms: Mock Service Worker — network level pe API intercept karta hai
MSW mein ek endpoint ka nakli response
lessons.what:
Definition: Do tarah ka mocking:

  • MSW — network level pe intercept. Tumhara code asli fetch call karta hai; MSW use pakad ke nakli response deta hai.
  • vi.mock — module level pe replace. Poora module nakli.

API ke liye MSW behtar hai.
lessons.why: vi.mock('./api') se tumhara asli fetch code, URL banana, headers, error handling — kuch bhi test nahi hota, kyunki wo poora module hi hata diya. MSW mein sirf network chhupa hai, baaki sab asli chalta hai. Aur wahi handlers dev mein bhi use ho sakte hain, aur browser mein bhi.
pros: MSW se asli fetch code test hota hai
Same handlers dev, test, aur Storybook mein
Error/slow/empty cases aasani se test
cons: MSW ka initial setup lagta hai
Handler aur asli API drift kar sakte hain
Zyada mocking se test asli behaviour se door chala jaata hai
gotchas: afterEach mein resetHandlers zaroor karo — warna ek test ka override agle test mein leak hoga
onUnhandledRequest:"error" set karo — chhoot gaya endpoint turant pata chalega
Handler ko asli API contract se match rakho, warna test pass par prod fail

lessons.name: Testing Custom Hooks
lessons.desc: renderHook from RTL wraps hooks in a minimal component so you can test stateful logic in isolation without building a full UI around it.
lessons.q: How do you test a custom hook that manages state and side effects? Walk through testing useFetch.
lessons.qsub: When should you test a hook directly vs testing it through a component that uses it?
terms: hook ko test mein chalane ka helper
state update ko wrap karna taaki React use process kar le
lessons.what:
Definition: Hooks ko akele test karne ke liye renderHook. Wo ek chhota component banata hai jo tumhara hook call karta hai, aur result.current se uski return value deta hai.

Par pehle sochо — agar hook kisi component mein use ho raha hai, to component ka test aksar zyada valuable hai.
lessons.why: Hook ka alag test tab worth hai jab wo reusable library-jaisa ho (useDebounce, usePagination, useLocalStorage) — bahut saari edge cases, kai consumers. App-specific hook ke liye component test hi kaafi hai.
pros: Hook ki edge cases seedhe test hoti hain
rerender se deps ka behaviour verify hota hai
Cleanup bugs pakde jaate hain
cons: result.current stale ho jaata hai — hamesha fresh padho
act() ka jhanjhat
Aksar component test se kam value
gotchas: result.current ko variable mein save mat karo — wo purana snapshot ho jaayega
Har state update act() ke andar honi chahiye, warna warning
App-specific hook ke liye component test likho, hook test nahi

lessons.name: Async Testing Patterns
lessons.desc: waitFor retries assertions until they pass or timeout. findBy queries are async. act() wraps state updates to ensure React flushes before assertions.
lessons.q: How do you test a component with async data loading? What is act() and when do you need it explicitly?
lessons.qsub: What causes the "not wrapped in act()" warning and how do you fix it properly (not just suppress it)?
terms: jab tak assertion pass na ho tab tak retry karta hai
timer ko nakli banana taaki test mein wait na karna pade
lessons.what:
Definition: React mein async kaam (fetch, timer, transition) ke baad DOM turant update nahi hota. RTL ke async tools:

  • findBy* — element aane ka intezaar (appear ke liye)
  • waitFor(fn) — koi bhi assertion pass hone tak retry
  • waitForElementToBeRemoved — spinner jaane ka intezaar
lessons.why: Flaky test ka #1 karan galat wait hai. setTimeout se wait karna sabse bura tarika hai — CI slow hoga to test random fail karega. findBy/waitFor polling karte hain: jaise hi condition sach hui, aage badh jaate hain — na zyada intezaar, na kam.
pros: Flakiness khatam
Test utna hi wait karta hai jitna zaroori
Fake timers se debounce test instant
cons: Fake timers + userEvent ka setup thoda tricky
waitFor ka default timeout (1s) kabhi kam pad jaata hai
act() warnings debug karna irritating hai
gotchas: setTimeout se manual wait KABHI mat karo — CI pe flaky ho jaayega
Fake timers use karo to userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers }) pass karo, warna hang
useRealTimers() afterEach mein zaroor — warna baaki tests tootenge

lessons.name: Why Next.js? — SSR, SSG, ISR & When to Use Each
lessons.desc: Next.js is the dominant React meta-framework. It adds server-side rendering (SSR), static site generation (SSG), incremental static regeneration (ISR), file-based routing, API routes, and built-in optimisations on top of React.
lessons.q: What problem does Next.js solve that create-react-app cannot? When would you choose SSR vs SSG vs ISR?
lessons.qsub: What is ISR and how does it differ from SSR? How does revalidation work?
terms: har request pe server HTML banata hai
build ke waqt HTML ban jaata hai
SSG + background mein time-time pe regenerate
lessons.what:
Definition: Next.js React ke upar ka framework hai — routing, rendering strategies, bundling, image optimization, API routes sab built-in.

Char rendering strategies:

  • SSG — build pe HTML. Sabse tez. Blog, docs, marketing.
  • ISR — SSG + har N second background refresh. Product pages, news.
  • SSR — har request pe fresh. Personalized dashboard.
  • CSR — client pe render. Admin panels, jahan SEO nahi chahiye.
lessons.why: Plain React (Vite) mein browser ko pehle khali HTML milta hai, phir JS download hota hai, phir data fetch hota hai, tab kuch dikhta hai. SEO crawler ko khali page milta hai aur mobile pe first paint slow hota hai. Next.js server pe HTML bana ke bhejta hai — content turant dikhta hai.

pros: Har page ki alag strategy — ek app mein sab mila sakte ho
SEO aur first paint bahut behtar
Routing, images, fonts sab built-in
cons: Vendor lock-in ka thoda risk (Vercel-optimized)
Learning curve — server/client ka batwara
Har release mein bade changes
gotchas: cookies() ya headers() use karte hi page dynamic (SSR) ho jaata hai — build pe static nahi rahega
SEO nahi chahiye to Next.js ka faayda kam hai — Vite se simple rahega
App Router aur Pages Router alag hain — tutorial dekhte waqt confirm karo kaunsa hai

lessons.name: App Router — File-Based Routing, Layouts & Loading States
lessons.desc: Next.js App Router (v13+) uses the app/ directory for file-based routing. Each folder is a route segment. layout.js persists across navigations, loading.js shows instant loading UI, error.js catches errors, and page.js defines the page content.
lessons.q: How does the App Router differ from the Pages Router? What are layouts, loading states, and error boundaries in the App Router?
lessons.qsub: What is parallel routing (@slot) and intercepting routes? When would you use them?
terms: folder structure hi URL structure hai
wo UI jo navigate karne pe bhi bana rehta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: App Router mein app/ folder ka structure hi routes hain. Special files:

  • page.tsx — us route ka UI
  • layout.tsx — wrapper jo navigate karne pe re-render nahi hota (state bacha rehta hai)
  • loading.tsx — apne aap Suspense boundary ban jaata hai
  • error.tsx — apne aap Error Boundary ban jaata hai (client component)
  • not-found.tsx, template.tsx, route.ts
lessons.why: Layouts nesting ka bada fayda hai — sidebar ka scroll position aur state navigate karne par bhi bacha rehta hai, kyunki layout unmount nahi hota. Aur loading.tsx/error.tsx se har route ko boundaries free mein mil jaati hain, manually likhne ki zaroorat nahi.
pros: Layout state navigate karne pe bacha rehta hai
loading/error boundaries automatic
Server Components default — bundle chhota
cons: Pages Router se poora alag — migration mehnat
Special files bahut saare, yaad rakhna padta hai
Caching behaviour version ke saath badalta rehta hai
gotchas: error.tsx mein "use client" zaroori hai, warna kaam nahi karega
Next 15 se params aur searchParams Promise hain — await karo
layout.tsx navigate karne pe re-render NAHI hota — har navigation pe kuch chahiye to template.tsx use karo

lessons.name: Server Components vs Client Components in Next.js
lessons.desc: In Next.js App Router, components are Server Components by default. They run only on the server, can directly access databases/filesystems, and send zero JS to the client. Add "use client" at the top to make a Client Component that runs in the browser.
lessons.q: What is the default rendering mode in Next.js App Router? How do you make a component interactive (Client Component)?
lessons.qsub: What can Server Components do that Client Components cannot? How do you pass server-fetched data to a Client Component?
terms: boundary jo us file se neeche sab client bana deti hai
jo JSON mein badla jaa sake — function nahi
server page ke andar chhota interactive hissa
lessons.what:
Definition: App Router mein sab kuch default Server Component hai. 'use client' likhne se wo file aur uske saare imports client bundle mein chale jaate hain.

Isliye rule: 'use client' ko tree mein jitna neeche ho sake utna neeche rakho — leaf ke paas.
lessons.analogy: Theatre. Stage server hai, sab kuch wahin set hota hai. Kuch interactive props (buttons) audience ke paas jaate hain — utne hi jitne zaroori.
lessons.why:
Sabse aam galti: 'use client' ko page ke top pe daal dena "kyunki ek button interactive chahiye tha". Isse poora page — saari libraries, saara data code — client bundle mein chala jaata hai aur RSC ka poora fayda khatam.

Sahi tarika: page server rahe, sirf <LikeButton> client ho.
pros: Client bundle bahut chhota
Secrets aur DB server pe safe
Data fetching waterfall kam
cons: Boundary galat lagayi to poora fayda khatam
Error messages confusing hote hain
Third-party libraries aksar "use client" maangti hain
gotchas: "use client" us file ke saare IMPORTS ko bhi client bundle mein le jaata hai
Server component ko client component mein import mat karo — children se pass karo
Client ko function props nahi ja sakte — sirf serializable data (aur Server Actions)

lessons.name: Data Fetching in Next.js — fetch(), Caching & Revalidation
lessons.desc: Next.js extends fetch() with built-in caching and revalidation. Server Components can async/await data directly. use cache: "force-cache" for SSG-like behaviour, or revalidate: 60 for ISR. Client components use React Query or SWR.
lessons.q: How does Next.js caching work with fetch()? What is the difference between force-cache and no-store?
lessons.qsub: How do you implement real-time data in Next.js? What are the gotchas of caching with dynamic routes?
terms: ek hi render mein same fetch = ek hi request
fetch ka result server pe cache — deployments ke beech bhi
cache kitni der baad refresh ho
lessons.what:
Definition: Server component mein tum seedha await fetch() ya DB call kar sakte ho. Next.js fetch ko extend karta hai:

  • cache: 'force-cache' — permanent cache
  • next: { revalidate: 60 } — 60s baad refresh (ISR)
  • cache: 'no-store' — har baar fresh (SSR)
  • next: { tags: ['posts'] } — tag se on-demand invalidate

Next 15 se default no-store hai — cache chahiye to explicitly maango.
lessons.why:
Request memoization prop drilling ki zaroorat khatam kar deta hai: layout aur page dono getUser() call karein to sirf ek HTTP request jaayegi. Isliye har component apna data khud maang sakta hai — waterfall ke bina.

Aur parallel fetching zaroori hai — sequential await waterfall banata hai.
pros: Component apna data khud maang sakta hai — prop drilling nahi
Cache layers built-in
Tag-based invalidation bahut powerful
cons: Caching ka mental model complex hai
Default behaviour version ke saath badla hai — confusion
Galat cache config se stale data production mein
gotchas: Next 15 se fetch default NO-CACHE hai — purane tutorials ulta batate hain
Sequential await = waterfall. Promise.all use karo.
DB/ORM calls fetch nahi hain — unke liye React ka cache() wrapper lagao

lessons.name: Hydration in Next.js — Mismatches, Selective Hydration & Streaming
lessons.desc: Hydration is when React attaches event handlers to server-rendered HTML. Next.js streams HTML with React Suspense boundaries — each boundary hydrates independently. Hydration mismatches (server HTML differs from client render) cause errors and hurt performance.
lessons.q: What is hydration? What causes hydration mismatches and how do you fix them?
lessons.qsub: How does selective hydration prioritise interactive content? What is the role of Suspense boundaries in streaming SSR?
terms: server HTML pe client JS jodkar use interactive banana
server aur client ka HTML alag hona
ek element ke liye warning band karna
lessons.what:
Definition: Server HTML bhejta hai (dikhta hai par interactive nahi). Phir JS aata hai aur React usi HTML pe apna tree "chipka" deta hai — event handlers lagata hai. Isko hydration kehte hain.

Mismatch tab hota hai jab client ka pehla render server ke HTML se alag nikle. React tab poora subtree phenk ke dobara banata hai — flicker + performance loss.
lessons.why:
Mismatch ki wajahein lagbhag hamesha yahi hoti hain: Date.now(), Math.random(), window/localStorage ka access, timezone/locale ka farak, ya browser extension ka DOM badalna.

Fix ka pattern ek hi hai: pehla render server jaisa hi rakho, aur browser-specific cheez useEffect mein (yaani doosre render mein) dikhao.

Dark mode ke liye flash-of-wrong-theme ka jhanjhat

Browser extensions (Grammarly) bhi mismatch dikha sakte hain — incognito mein verify karo

lessons.name: Next.js Image, Font & Metadata Optimisations
lessons.desc: next/image automatically optimises images (lazy loading, responsive sizing, WebP/AVIF, CDN). next/font optimises font loading (self-hosted, no FOUT, layout-shift-free). Metadata API handles SEO (title, description, Open Graph, structured data).
lessons.q: How does next/image differ from a regular img tag? What optimisations does it perform?
lessons.qsub: How do you handle dynamic metadata for dynamic routes? What is generateMetadata()?
terms: Cumulative Layout Shift — page ka kood-na
Largest Contentful Paint — sabse bada content kab dikha
Flash of Unstyled Text — font load hone se pehle default font dikhna
lessons.what:
Definition: Next.js ke built-in optimizers:

  • next/image — automatic resize, WebP/AVIF, lazy load, blur placeholder
  • next/font — font build time pe self-host, zero layout shift
  • metadata export — SEO tags server pe
  • next/script — third-party scripts ka loading control
lessons.why: Ye teeno seedha Core Web Vitals pe asar karte hain (jo Google ranking mein count hote hain). Image bina width/height ke CLS deta hai; Google Fonts CDN se aaye to extra DNS + connection + FOUT; metadata client pe set ho to crawler ko dikhta hi nahi.
where: next/font — Google Fonts link kabhi mat use karo
pros: Core Web Vitals apne aap behtar
Font self-hosted — external request nahi
Images automatically WebP/AVIF mein convert
cons: next/image ka self-hosted setup (sharp) config maangta hai
External images ke liye domain whitelist karna padta hai
Vercel ke bahar image optimization ka apna cost
gotchas: Above-the-fold image pe priority lagao — warna wo lazy load hoke LCP kharab karegi
fill use karo to parent pe position:relative aur sizes prop zaroori hai
Google Fonts <link> se mat lao — next/font se lao, warna FOUT aur extra request

lessons.name: API Routes & Server Actions
lessons.desc: API routes (app/api/) let you build backend endpoints inside your Next.js app. Server Actions (v14+) let you call async functions directly from form actions and Server Components without creating API routes — handling mutations server-side.
lessons.q: When would you use API routes vs Server Actions? What are the trade-offs?
lessons.qsub: How does progressive enhancement work with Server Actions? How do you handle validation and errors in Server Actions?
terms: server pe chalne wala function jo client se call ho sakta hai
directive jo function ko Server Action banata hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Do tarike server pe kaam karne ke:

  • Route Handler — app/api/x/route.ts mein GET/POST export karo. Ye asli HTTP endpoint hai — mobile app, webhook, external client sab call kar sakte hain.
  • Server Action — 'use server' wala async function jise tum seedha form ya button se call kar sakte ho. Next.js beech ka HTTP khud handle karta hai.
lessons.why:
Server Action se poora "API route banao → fetch likho → loading state manage karo → error handle karo" wala boilerplate khatam ho jaata hai. Aur form JavaScript ke bina bhi kaam karta hai (progressive enhancement) — kyunki wo asli HTML form submit hai.

Route handler tab chahiye jab endpoint bahar se bhi call ho — webhook, mobile app, cron.
pros: Server Action se boilerplate lagbhag zero
Form JS ke bina bhi chalta hai
revalidatePath se cache turant refresh
cons: Server Action ek public endpoint hai — security khud handle karni padti hai
Debugging mushkil — network tab mein saaf nahi dikhta
Sirf Next.js — portable nahi
gotchas: Server Action PUBLIC endpoint hai — har action mein auth check aur input validation KHUD karo
Server Action ka return serializable hona chahiye
Mutation ke baad revalidatePath/revalidateTag zaroor karo, warna user ko purana data dikhega

lessons.name: Deploying Next.js — Vercel, Docker & Edge Runtime
lessons.desc: Vercel is the default deployment platform (built by Next.js creators). For self-hosting: standalone output mode + Docker. Edge Runtime runs middleware and API routes at the edge (CDN nodes) for low latency. Static export for fully static sites.
lessons.q: What is the difference between deploying on Vercel vs self-hosting with Docker? What is Edge Runtime?
lessons.qsub: How do you configure Next.js for a monorepo? What is the standalone output mode?
terms: user ke paas wale server pe chalna — tez par limited APIs
poora Node.js — sab kuch chalta hai
build output jisme sirf zaroori files hoti hain — Docker ke liye
lessons.what:
Definition: Next.js kai jagah deploy ho sakta hai:

  • Vercel — zero config, sab features (ISR, image optimization, edge) kaam karte hain
  • Docker / self-host — output: 'standalone' se chhoti image
  • Static export — output: 'export', par SSR/ISR/API sab band

Edge vs Node: Edge tez aur user ke paas hai par Node APIs (fs, crypto ke kuch hisse, most DB drivers) nahi chalte.
lessons.why: Self-host karte waqt log atakte hain kyunki ISR ko persistent filesystem chahiye, image optimization ko sharp chahiye, aur multiple instances mein cache share nahi hota. Ye pehle se jaan lo to architecture sahi banega.
pros: standalone se Docker image bahut chhoti
Edge runtime se global latency kam
Static export CDN pe lagbhag muft
cons: Self-host mein ISR/image optimization extra kaam maangte hain
Edge runtime mein bahut saari libraries nahi chalti
Vercel ke bahar kuch features ka support kam
gotchas: NEXT_PUBLIC_ wale env browser mein dikhte hain — secret kabhi mat daalo
Env variables BUILD time pe inline hote hain — runtime pe badalne ke liye rebuild chahiye
Edge runtime mein Prisma jaise DB clients nahi chalte — pehle check karo

lessons.name: React Router — nested routes, loaders, actions, data APIs
lessons.desc: React Router v6.4+ (Remix merger) adds data APIs: loaders for server-side data fetching, actions for form mutations, useNavigation for pending states. Nested routes with outlet. Layout routes for shared UI. Error boundaries for route-level errors.
lessons.q: How does React Router v6 data API differ from useEffect-based data fetching?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between loaders and useEffect for data fetching? How do nested routes work with outlets?
terms: route ke andar route — layout ke saath
route ka data render se PEHLE laane wala function
form submission handle karne wala function
lessons.what:
Definition: React Router SPA ka routing solution hai. v6.4+ se usme data APIs aa gaye — loader (data pehle laao), action (form handle karo), errorElement (route-level error boundary).

Isse "render karo phir fetch karo" waterfall khatam hota hai — data aur code parallel load hote hain.
lessons.why: Purana pattern: component render → useEffect → fetch → spinner → data. Nested routes mein ye waterfall banta hai (parent load hoke hi child shuru hota hai). Loader ke saath router saare matching routes ke loaders parallel chala deta hai — data pehle se ready hota hai.
pros: Loaders se waterfall khatam — parallel data
Route-level error boundaries built-in
Nested layouts natural
cons: v5 se v6 aur data APIs — bahut breaking changes
Tutorials aksar purane version ke
SSR ke liye alag setup (Remix)
gotchas: Nested route ke liye parent mein <Outlet /> zaroori hai, warna child dikhega hi nahi
Loader mein Response throw karo (Error nahi) taaki status code sahi mile
v6 mein "exact" prop nahi hai — matching ab default exact hai

lessons.name: React Forms — controlled vs uncontrolled, validation, React Hook Form, Formik
lessons.desc: Controlled: React state owns value (onChange + value). Uncontrolled: DOM owns value (useRef + defaultValue). React Hook Form uses uncontrolled for performance with validation. Formik provides controlled model with built-in validation. Server Actions handle form state in Next.js.
lessons.q: When would you use uncontrolled over controlled components? What are the performance implications?
lessons.qsub: How does React Hook Form achieve performance? What is the difference between formik and react-hook-form?
terms: uncontrolled inputs pe based fast form library
validation schema (zod/yup) ko RHF se jodne wala adapter
RHF mein input ko form se jodna
lessons.what:
Definition: Form banane ke 3 raste:

  • Controlled useState — chhote forms (1-3 fields) ke liye theek
  • React Hook Form — uncontrolled + refs. Har keystroke pe re-render nahi hota. Bade forms ka default.
  • Formik — purana, controlled based. Naye projects mein RHF behtar.
lessons.why:
30 fields ka controlled form har keystroke pe poora form re-render karta hai — typing lag karti hai. RHF inputs ko uncontrolled rakhta hai aur refs se value padhta hai, isliye typing pe koi re-render hi nahi hota. Sirf error dikhne ya submit pe render hota hai.

Aur zod ke saath schema ek jagah likhne se type + validation dono mil jaate hain.
pros: Typing pe zero re-render — bada form bhi fast
zod se validation aur TS type ek jagah
Error messages, touched, dirty sab built-in
cons: Custom components ke liye Controller wrap karna padta hai
Uncontrolled ka mental model alag hai
Dependent fields (ek field doosre pe depend) thoda tricky
gotchas: {...register("x")} spread karna zaroori hai — sirf name dena kaam nahi karega
MUI/Radix jaise controlled components ke liye Controller use karo
defaultValues zaroor do, warna "uncontrolled to controlled" warning aayegi

lessons.name: Error Boundaries — catch render errors, fallback UI, componentDidCatch
lessons.desc: Error boundaries catch JavaScript errors in their child component tree during rendering, lifecycle methods, and constructors. They don't catch errors in event handlers, async code, or server-side rendering. Use getDerivedStateFromError for state update, componentDidCatch for logging.
lessons.q: What do Error Boundaries catch and what don't they catch? How do you implement one?
lessons.qsub: How do you log errors from Error Boundaries to an error reporting service? Can you use multiple Error Boundaries nested?
terms: popular library — reset aur hooks ke saath
error ke waqt dikhne wala UI
wo value jiske badalne pe boundary apne aap reset ho
lessons.what:
Definition: Raw class boundary sirf error pakadti hai — reset ka koi tarika nahi deti. Practice mein tumhe chahiye: retry button, route badalne pe apne aap reset, aur error logging.

react-error-boundary library ye sab deti hai — onReset, resetKeys, aur useErrorBoundary hook (async errors ko boundary tak pahunchane ke liye).
lessons.why: Async errors sabse bada gap hai. fetch fail ho to boundary use nahi pakadti — tumhe khud state mein rakh ke render karna padta hai. useErrorBoundary().showBoundary(err) se tum us error ko boundary tak pahuncha sakte ho, taaki error handling ek hi jagah rahe.
pros: Retry ka option user ko milta hai
resetKeys se navigation pe apne aap reset
Async errors bhi ek hi jagah handle
cons: Ek aur dependency
Reset logic soch samajh ke likhna padta hai (warna infinite retry loop)
Event handler errors abhi bhi manual
gotchas: onReset mein wahi cheez retry karo jo faili thi — warna reset hote hi phir crash
resetKeys mein route/id daalo taaki navigate karne pe purana error na chipke
Error boundary dev mein error phir bhi console mein dikhata hai — ye normal hai

lessons.name: prop-types, defaultProps, refs callback pattern
lessons.desc: prop-types: runtime type checking (legacy, replaced by TypeScript). defaultProps: default values for undefined props (deprecated in function components, use default parameters instead). refs callback: function refs for custom logic on mount/unmount.
lessons.q: Why are defaultProps deprecated for function components? What replaces them?
lessons.qsub: How do you implement a callback ref pattern? What is the difference between useRef and callback refs?
terms: runtime pe props check karne wali purani library
props ki default value dene ka purana tarika
ref ki jagah function dena — mount/unmount pe chalta hai
lessons.what:
Definition: Teen legacy cheezein jo interview mein aati hain:

  • PropTypes — runtime type check. TypeScript ke saamne aaj bekaar. React 19 mein hata diya gaya.
  • defaultProps — function components ke liye deprecated. Ab JS default parameters use karo.
  • Callback ref — abhi bhi useful, aur React 19 mein cleanup function bhi support karta hai.
lessons.why: Ye jaanna zaroori hai kyunki (a) purane codebases mein ye milega, (b) interview mein "PropTypes vs TypeScript" poocha jaata hai, aur (c) callback ref aaj bhi ek asli tool hai jab tumhe node ke mount/unmount pe kuch karna ho — useRef se ye nahi hota kyunki ref badalne pe koi notification nahi milti.
where: callback ref se mount pe measure
pros: Callback ref se mount/unmount pe reliably kaam kar sakte ho
Default parameters PropTypes se saaf aur type-safe
TypeScript compile time pe pakadta hai — runtime cost zero
cons: PropTypes ka runtime check TS ke saath duplicate kaam tha
Inline callback ref memo ke bina har render chalta hai
defaultProps class components mein abhi bhi chalte hain — confusion
gotchas: React 19 mein PropTypes aur function components ke defaultProps dono hata diye gaye
Callback ref ko useCallback mein wrap karo, warna har render pe null + node ke saath do baar chalega
TypeScript compile time hai — API se aaya data usse verify nahi hota, uske liye zod chahiye
